chapters.title: 천만 회 다음 날의 셀카 폭격

arcs.title: 불을 끄려 할수록 밝아지는 신사
arcs.promise: 들키지 않으려 빛을 낮추면 지켜진다고 믿던 베스퍼가 인간 공범을 얻는다. 그러나 억누른 빛이 오히려 더 큰 시선을 부르는 것을 직접 겪고, 다음 해법으로 시선을 떠넘기는 쪽을 택한다.

arcs.title: 시선을 넘긴 밤들
arcs.promise: 숨으려고 칸드라에게 시선을 넘긴 문지기가, 그 빛값을 칸드라의 초와 다온의 기록이 대신 치르는 것을 본다. 그 끝에 공연 중에는 더 이상 문을 지킬 수 없는 자리까지 밀려난다.

arcs.title: 폐장 뒤의 가로등
arcs.promise: 공연 중 문을 지킬 길이 막힌 문지기는 밤마다 혼자 빛을 태워 이긴다. 그 승리가 낮의 흐림과 남의 이름으로 되돌아오는 것을 겪으며, 아무도 들이지 않던 순찰길에 처음으로 한 사람의 발소리를 허락한다. 그리고 묻지 않는 대신 불을 낮춰 곁에 머무는 쪽을 스스로 고른다.

arcs.title: 가장자리에서 온 촛불
arcs.promise: 곁을 허락하기 시작한 문지기가 위협의 정체와 칸드라가 넘어온 이유를 마주한다. 그는 지키려고 밀어내는 방식도 결국 혼자 짊어지기의 다른 얼굴임을 겪는다. 동시에 제 판단으로 움직이던 다온은 그 판단이 연달아 제 기록으로 되돌아오는 한계에 부딪힌다.

arcs.title: 핼러윈 주말, 가장 넓은 문
arcs.promise: 말을 삼켜 곁을 지키던 문지기와, 혼자 이름을 걸던 공범이 판단을 나누기 시작한다. 그 끝에서 베스퍼는 혼자의 불빛으로는 문을 막을 수 없다고 처음으로 입 밖에 낸다.

arcs.title: 도와주시오, 그리고 빛의 방패
arcs.promise: 혼자 빛을 낮추고 막던 문지기가 처음으로 도움을 청한다. 사람들의 빛이 모여 방패가 되는 밤을 겪고, 문을 닫는 값이 결국 자기 불꽃이라는 사실 앞에 선다.

arcs.title: 나눈 불, 남는 자리
arcs.promise: 사명의 셈 뒤에 욕망을 숨기던 문지기가 제 불을 나누겠다고 먼저 말한다. 끝까지 혼자 타 없어지려던 레이디는 누군가 오래 들여다보는 불을 받아들인다. 마지막 밤의 선택은 네 사람이 각자 건 값 위에서 내려진다.

episodes.title: 천만 회 다음 날의 셀카 폭격

units.text: 대기 공간 천막 아래에는 늘 퍼레이드 직전의 냄새가 고여 있었다. 분장용 스프레이와 식은 츄러스 설탕 냄새, 그리고 발전기 기름 냄새였다.
베스퍼는 그 한가운데에 허리를 곧게 펴고 서 있었다. 키가 이 미터 가까이 되다 보니 천막 지붕 이음새가 등갓 바로 위에서 펄럭였다. 그는 조심스럽게 고개를 한 치쯤 숙였다.
"천만이래, 천만. 하루 만에."
"가스등 오빠 미쳤다니까. 댓글 봐, '저 탈 안에 무용 전공자 있음'이래."
스태프 몇이 휴대폰을 맞대고 킥킥거렸다. 작은 검은 판 속에서 누군가가 빛나고 있었다. 황동 테두리와 유리 등갓, 그 안에서 활활 타는 불꽃. 관객에게 손등 인사를 하느라 허리를 반쯤 접은 모습이었다.
자기였다.
베스퍼는 그 '천만'이 무엇을 센 숫자인지 정확히 알지 못했다. 다만 어젯밤 퍼레이드가 끝난 뒤로 사람들이 그를 보는 눈길이 한 겹 두꺼워졌다는 것만은 알았다. 문지기는 두꺼운 눈길에 걸려서는 안 되는 존재였다.
그는 숨을 가늘게 들이쉬고 불꽃을 눌렀다. 호박색 빛이 촛농 한 방울 떨어질 동안 천천히 줄어들어, 바람 부는 밤의 골목등쯤이 되었다.
이만하면 배경이다.

findings.ko: 2·4칸 가운데 스태프 엑스트라가 반묶음 단발, 남색 재킷, 눈썹 옆 점으로 그려져 다음 장면부터 나오는 한다온 기준 이미지와 닮아 보입니다.
findings.en: The central staff extra in panels 2 and 4 has a half-up dark bob, navy jacket and a small mole near the eyebrow, which reads close to the Han Daon reference although Daon does not appear until the next scenes.

findings.ko: 5칸의 불꽃이 아직 꽤 커서, 바람 부는 골목 가로등처럼 흐려진 느낌은 6칸에서야 분명해집니다.
findings.en: The flame in panel 5 is still fairly large; the windy-alley-lamp dimness reads more clearly only in panel 6.

plan.intent: The reader moves from the cozy, crowded backstage tent to Vesper's quiet alarm. Staff giggle over a viral clip of the lamp-headed gentleman, and he is the one in it. Vesper does not understand the number, but he does understand that the looks have thickened. The comedy stays soft; the dramatic turn is his private decision to hide. He deliberately presses his own flame down to the dimness of a windy alley lamp and judges that this is enough to be background. The scene should end on the dimmed flame, a small self-erasure that the reader feels as both funny and a little sad.
plan.staging: Interior of the backstage waiting tent, before the evening parade. Vesper stands near the center of the tent. His lamp head sits just below the tent roof seam, which flaps close above the shade; his head is dipped slightly. The staff huddle is somewhere in the same tent, near enough that Vesper can take in their talk and see the screen. Their exact distance and direction from him are open. Their phones are held together, with a small screen showing a clip of Vesper glowing mid-bow. The screen carries no UI labels or readable text. The spoken lines in text-2 and text-3 must use balloons with tails to the unnamed staff huddle, never narrator boxes, even though the speaker field reads narrator. Which staff member says which line is open. Only ordinary human staff are present besides Vesper. Kandra, Daon and Taerim do not appear. Across the scene, Vesper's flame goes from its normal amber glow to a clearly smaller, dimmer amber, comparable to an alley lamp on a windy night. The source does not state a color change, only a loss of brightness. The camera, panel division and where the dimming is shown are left to the artist.
uncertainties: The source does not identify or count the staff who speak ch-1-p-3 and ch-1-p-4. They are unregistered extras, so the speaker field uses narrator only because of validator limits; these lines are spoken dialogue from the staff, not narration. Whether one person or two speak is also unknown.
The source does not say whether the staff notice that Vesper is standing nearby, or whether anyone notices his flame dimming.

The source does not state how Vesper physically presses the flame down beyond a thin breath. No gesture, strain or visible mechanism should be invented. World fact wf4 says forced dimming cannot last long, but this scene does not show it failing.
The duration in ch-1-p-8 is given as the time of one wax drop falling, an in-world measure, not a clock time.
The exact time of this scene is unstated. It is only implied to be after last night's parade and before a parade, since the tent smells of the moment before a parade.
Whether Vesper understands the dance-major comment, or knows the nickname used for him, is not stated. The source only says he does not know what the ten million counted.
The number ten million is not explicitly called view count in this excerpt. The screen should not display a number or label.

beats.action: The backstage tent is established: pre-parade clutter and smell. Vesper stands upright at its center, so tall the flapping roof seam nearly brushes his lamp shade. He dips his head a fraction, politely making room for the tent.
Nearby, a small huddle of staff put their phones together and giggle. They trade excited lines about ten million views in a day and a comment about a dance major inside the costume.
The phone screen is revealed. It shows the lamp-headed gentleman blazing bright, bent half at the waist in a back-of-hand greeting to the crowd. The narration confirms the figure is Vesper himself.

Vesper does not understand what the number counts. He does register that people's gazes on him have thickened since last night. He recalls that a gatekeeper must not be caught in such gazes, and this moves him from bystander to someone deciding to act.

Vesper breathes in thinly and deliberately presses his flame down. The amber glow dwindles slowly to the dimness of a windy-night alley lamp. He concludes privately that this is enough to pass as background.

facts.statement: The scene is under the waiting-area tent. It always smells like the moment before the parade: makeup spray, cold churro sugar and generator oil.
Vesper stands in the middle of the tent with his back straight. He is close to two meters tall, so the tent roof seam flaps just above his lamp shade. He carefully lowers his head by a tiny amount.

Several staff members have their phones pressed together and are giggling. They say something reached ten million in one day and quote a comment claiming there is a dance major inside the costume. These lines belong to unnamed staff extras, not to any registered character.

On the small black screen, a figure is glowing: a brass frame, a glass shade and a blazing flame inside. The figure is bent halfway at the waist, giving the audience a back-of-hand greeting. The figure is Vesper himself.

Vesper does not know exactly what the ten million counted. He only knows that since last night's parade ended, the way people look at him has grown one layer thicker. He also believes a gatekeeper is a being who must not get caught in thick looks.

Vesper takes a thin breath and presses his flame down. The amber light shrinks slowly, over about the time one drop of candle wax takes to fall, until it is about as bright as an alley lamp on a windy night.
Vesper judges that at this level he counts as background.

brief.style: Full-color Korean romance-fantasy comedy webtoon, clean expressive linework, soft cel shading, warm night palette with Vesper's amber gas-lamp flame as key light.

moments.action: Cluttered backstage parade tent with equipment cases and a generator. Very tall Vesper stands straight at center, lamp head dipped slightly beneath the flapping roof seam, flame glowing normal amber.
A small huddle of ordinary human staff press their phones together, giggling excitedly. Speech balloons tail to the staff.
Close on the small phone screen held in staff hands. It shows only a glowing brass-framed lamp-headed gentleman, flame blazing, bent halfway at the waist in a back-of-hand greeting to a crowd.
Vesper stands very still near the giggling staff, lamp head slightly dipped, flame at normal amber, quietly unsettled.
Vesper holds still as his amber flame shrinks inside the glass shade, visibly lower and softer than before.
Vesper in the busy tent, his lamp now a small dim amber flame like a windy-night alley lamp. Thought balloon linked to his glass lamp head.

review.evidence: Six panels read top to bottom: wide tent shot with Vesper standing tall among costume racks and equipment cases; staff huddle giggling over a phone; the phone screen showing Vesper bowing with a back-of-hand greeting to a crowd; Vesper looking toward the giggling staff; close-up of his lamp head with a small amber flame and the upper-left crack visible; Vesper from behind with the dimmed flame and a thought bubble. All eight quoted lines are verbatim with no invented text or name labels.

units.text: "요즘 당신 불이 너무 작아요."
옆에서 칸드라가 말했다. 상아색 초 꼭대기의 불꽃이 그를 향해 살짝 기울어 있었다. 늘 곧게 서던 불이 오늘은 자꾸 옆으로 누웠다. 베스퍼는 그것을 먼저 보았지만 묻지 않았다. 대신 자기 불을 한 번 더 낮췄다.
"어제 그 영상 때문이죠? 사람들이 당신더러 오빠래요, 오빠."
"오빠라는 것은 어떤 직위요?"
"음, 그건 나중에요. 아무튼 그렇게 줄이면 멀리서는 꺼진 줄 알겠어요."
"전혀 개의치 않소, 레이디. 오늘 밤 나는 조명 소품 하나에 지나지 않을 것이오."
말은 반듯했다.
등갓 안의 불꽃이 분홍색으로 세 번 깜빡였다.
칸드라가 손으로 입을 가렸다. 웃음이 새어 나오는 모양이었다. 베스퍼는 목깃을 바로잡는 척 고개를 돌렸다. 걱정받는 게 반갑다는 사실까지 불빛이 떠벌릴 필요는 없었다.

findings.ko: 4칸의 분홍 불꽃 안에 웃는 눈과 입이 그려졌습니다. 원문은 감정을 불빛 색과 깜박임으로만 보여 줍니다.
findings.en: Panel 4 draws smiling eyes and mouth inside the pink flame; the source shows his emotion through color and blinking only.

findings.en: In panel 1 the narration caption is placed above Kandra's balloon, so it is read before her line, although the source puts her line first.

plan.intent: This picks up right after Vesper dimmed his flame to hide. The reader should feel the joke turn tender. Kandra, beside him, notices the dimness and teases him about the viral nickname. Vesper answers with stiff, formal dignity, but his own flame betrays him by blinking pink. The comedy lives in the gap between his upright words and his traitorous light. Under the comedy sit two quiet signals. Kandra's flame keeps leaning sideways, a sign of unease; Vesper sees it and deliberately does not ask. By the end both are hiding something small from each other and the reader senses it, even though neither says it.
plan.staging: Same backstage waiting tent as the previous scene, continuous in time: Vesper has just dimmed his flame, and it stays small and dim amber throughout, never fully out. Kandra stands beside Vesper, close enough to converse quietly; which side she stands on is open. Vesper is far taller than Kandra. Kandra's head is one thick ivory pillar candle with hardened wax drips and exactly ONE wick carrying exactly ONE flame in every panel; never two wicks or two flames. Her candle has no face: no mouth, eyes or smile marks drawn on the wax. Emotion shows only through the flame and body language. In the opening exchange her single flame leans sideways, tilted toward Vesper, rather than standing upright. Reading order in the opening moment: Kandra's line text-1 must be read before the narration caption text-2, so place her balloon first in the reading path and the caption after it. Vesper has no mouth; his balloons point to the glass lamp head. The pink three-blink happens inside his glass shade and is the comedic peak; the source gives the color pink and the count three, and nothing else about the mechanism. At the close, Kandra's hand is raised to the lower front of her candle where a mouth would be, without drawing a mouth, and Vesper's head is turned away while a gloved hand works at his collar. No other named characters appear. Unnamed staff may exist in the background as ordinary humans but do not speak. No readable text anywhere except the listed lines; no speaker labels. Camera choices, panel division and where each beat lands are left to the artist.
uncertainties: The source does not say which side of Vesper Kandra stands on, or how far apart they are beyond being beside each other.
Whether other staff are still nearby in the tent, or whether anyone besides Kandra sees the pink blinking, is not stated.
The source says the laughter only seems to be leaking out (ch-1-p-18 is phrased as appearance); whether Kandra is laughing aloud is unknown, so no laughter sfx should be added.
Kandra has no mouth, yet ch-1-p-18 says she covers her mouth with her hand; the gesture should be read as a hand raised to where a mouth would be, without inventing facial features.
How far Vesper lowers his flame the second time is not quantified. Kandra's warning in ch-1-p-14 implies it only risks looking extinguished from afar; it does not go out.

The source does not explain why Kandra's flame leans. Per the character's emotion code a sideways lean signals unease, but the cause is deliberately hidden and must not be shown or hinted beyond the lean itself.
Pink is not in Vesper's registered light-color code; the source states pink directly for this moment and it should be used as written without inventing a meaning label.
The nickname in ch-1-p-12 is left unexplained on purpose; Kandra defers it, so no visual gloss or explanation should be added.
The exact clock time is unstated; it is before tonight's parade, continuing from the previous scene.

beats.action: Kandra, at Vesper's side, remarks on how small his light has become. Her single flame leans sideways toward him instead of standing straight. Vesper sees the lean, chooses not to ask, and quietly dims his own flame one notch further.
Kandra shifts to teasing: it must be yesterday's video, and people are calling him by the affectionate nickname. Vesper, earnest and literal, asks what rank that is.

Kandra waves the question off for later and warns that from a distance his light will look extinguished. Vesper answers with formal composure that he does not mind and will be a mere lighting prop tonight.
The narration grants that his words were proper. Then his flame betrays him: it blinks pink three times inside the glass shade.

Kandra covers the lower front of her candle with her hand, laughter leaking out. Vesper turns his lamp head aside, fussing with his collar, embarrassed that his light gave away his gladness at being worried about.

facts.statement: Kandra, standing beside Vesper, speaks first. She tells him his light has been far too small lately.
The flame on top of Kandra's ivory candle is tilted slightly toward Vesper. It usually stands straight, but today it keeps lying over to the side.
Vesper notices the leaning flame first but does not ask about it. Instead he lowers his own flame one more time.
Kandra guesses it is because of yesterday's video and tells him people are calling him by a Korean affectionate term for an older man, repeating the term twice.
Vesper asks what kind of rank or position that term is.
Kandra defers the explanation to later. She warns that if he shrinks his light like that, people far away will think it has gone out.
Vesper replies that he does not mind at all, addressing her as lady, and says that tonight he will be nothing more than a lighting prop.
His words are proper and upright, but the flame inside his lamp shade blinks pink three times.

Kandra covers the place of her mouth with her hand, apparently because laughter is leaking out. Vesper turns his head away, pretending to straighten his collar. He feels his light did not need to broadcast that he is glad to be worried about.

plan.intent: The quiet, embarrassed moment between Vesper and Kandra is broken by a rushing staff member, and the scene becomes workplace comedy. Han Daon, a new hire, bursts in with a radio and delivers a fast, number-heavy briefing. She repeats the three-minute limit several times and ends by asking for his agreement. Vesper answers with an archaic, courtly acceptance, treating her instruction as a command. Daon stalls on the unfamiliar word and then accepts it, repeating it. The humor comes from her modern, clock-driven speech meeting his old-fashioned courtesy. Underneath, the reader learns that Vesper stretched yesterday's selfie zone to seven minutes, a small figure that hints at future exposure risk. The narration keeps a slightly distant, uncertain view of Daon, as if Vesper barely knows her yet.

Daon turns to Vesper and delivers the selfie-zone rule quickly. She hammers the three-minute limit and cites yesterday's seven-minute overrun that backed up the line. She closes with a request for his agreement.
Vesper accepts with courtly formality. Daon stalls on his archaic word, then goes along with it and repeats it back.

facts.statement: Someone calls out to the gentleman and the candle performer that standby is five minutes away.

A staff member with half-up tied hair runs into the tent holding a radio. Her name tag bears the name Han Daon. The narration recalls, without certainty, that everyone seemed to call her the new hire.
She tells Vesper that today's C-zone selfie zone is three minutes. She repeats three and says it is not four.
She explains that yesterday he did seven minutes and the parade line behind was pushed back. She asks him to cut it off cleanly today and seeks his agreement.
Vesper replies that he will do as commanded, using an archaic phrase that treats her instruction as an order.

units.text: 여덟 시 이십 분.
인간의 시계는 볼 줄 몰라도 베스퍼의 몸은 그 순간을 알았다. 발밑에서 음악이 차오르고, 조명이 한꺼번에 켜지고, 동선 저 끝 어딘가에서 문이 크게 숨을 들이쉬는 순간이었다.
행렬이 움직였다.
"가등 선생님!"
"가스등 오빠 여기 좀 봐 주세요!"
함성이 파도처럼 밀려와 등갓에 부딪혔다. 불꽃이 저절로 솟으려 했다. 베스퍼는 속으로 수를 세며 그것을 눌러 앉혔다. 배경이다. 소품이다. 가로등은 원래 말이 없다.
C구간에 들어서자 음악이 느려지고 행렬이 멈췄다. 셀카존이었다.
맨 앞의 젊은 여인이 검은 판을 두 손으로 내밀었다.
"저, 사진 한 장만 같이 찍어 주시면 안 될까요?"
베스퍼는 그 판을 내려다보았다. 어제도 그는 이 의식을 스물몇 번 치렀다. 인간들은 판을 얼굴 앞에 들고 무언가를 '담는다'고 했다. 담는다면 무엇을 담는가. 문 너머의 오래된 이야기에는 그림자를 떼어 가는 거울이 있었다. 이것도 그런 종류일지 몰랐다.
하지만 숙녀분이 정중히 청했다. 청을 거절하는 것은 무례였다.
"영광이오, 숙녀분."
그는 모자를 벗는 시늉으로 허리를 숙이고 몸을 기울였다. 판이 등갓 바로 앞까지 다가왔다. 베스퍼는 불꽃의 색을 아주 조금 희게 틀었다. 화면 속 그의 얼굴 자리에 부드러운 빛이 번지면서 황동 이음새와 목 아래의 텅 빈 어둠이 하얗게 지워졌다.
"와, 빛 번짐 감성 미쳤다. 진짜 영화 같아요!"
칭찬이 등갓을 톡 두드렸다. 불꽃이 한 단계 밝아졌다.

plan.intent: The 8:20 parade begins, and the reader feels it through Vesper's body rather than a clock: music rising, lights snapping on, the door far down the route drawing breath. Fans shout his nicknames, and the cheering pushes his flame upward on its own. He counts silently and forces it back down, telling himself he is only scenery. At the C-zone selfie stop a young woman politely holds out her phone. Vesper quietly weighs the device against an old tale of a mirror that steals shadows. His etiquette wins over his caution, because refusing a polite request would be rude. He bows and tints his flame slightly whiter so the phone image blurs away the brass seams and the empty dark below his collar. That hides him from the camera, but her delighted praise makes his flame brighten one step anyway. The comedy and the tension come from the same place: his light obeys his feelings more than his duty. Narration is split into short, separate captions so each line can be lettered large and exactly.
plan.staging:
Same night parade route as the previous finished attempt, starting at the moment the 8:20 parade begins and ending at the C-zone selfie stop. Keep that staging.

Only Vesper and Kandra have lamp and candle heads. All other parade performers are ordinary humans in gothic costumes; fans, the young woman and any staff are ordinary people. Kandra is present in the procession near Vesper but does not speak and has no scripted action here. Her head is one thick ivory pillar candle with hardened wax drips, exactly one wick and one flame, and no drawn face.

Vesper is far taller than the humans. His glass lamp head shows no face, eyes or mouth; emotion shows only through flame brightness, color and posture. The crack on the upper left of the glass stays visible. His speech balloon (text-15) points to his lamp head. His thoughts (text-9, text-12) are thought balloons or thought-style captions tied to him.

Fan shouts (text-4, text-5) come from unnamed fans behind the rope line; tails point into the crowd, not to any named character. text-11 and text-17 are spoken by the same young woman at the front of the crowd; tails point to her.

Required causal order: flame tries to rise (text-6) before the counting and suppression captions (text-7, text-8). text-7 and text-8 are two separate short captions, read in that order. text-13 is its own caption, not merged with any other line. text-14 comes before his reply text-15.

The phone: the woman holds it out with both hands; during the photo it comes right up to his lamp glass. If the phone screen is shown, it displays a soft white glow where his face would be, with the brass seams and the dark space below his collar washed out to white. No UI, icons or lettering on the screen.

The flame whitening in beat 5 is a very slight shift, not a dramatic flash. The brightening in beat 6 is one step up from that.

The mirror in text-13 is part of an old tale; do not draw scenery of the world beyond the door. Whether to show any mirror image at all is left to the artist.

No readable text beyond the listed lines, no speaker names or labels, no signs or brand marks. Panel division, camera and beat placement are the artist's choice; prefer fewer, larger panels with large, crisp captions.
uncertainties: The door's exact location on the route and what 'taking a breath' looks like are not described in ch-1-p-26. Do not invent a visible door or effect; it may stay off-panel.
Vesper's flame color while suppressing in ch-1-p-30 is not stated. The source says only that he presses it down; no new color meaning should be assigned.

Daon does not appear in this excerpt; whether she is on the route is unknown and she should not be given any action.
The source does not say whether the photo is taken as a selfie from the woman's arm or by another person; only that the device came right up to his lamp glass.
The source does not say whether the woman or anyone notices the whitening. Only the washed-out screen result and her praise are stated.
Whether the brighter flame in ch-1-p-39 is caught by the camera or causes any exposure risk is not stated in this excerpt.
The previous scene's staff instruction about a three-minute limit is not referenced here; do not show a timer or imply a timing violation.

beats.action: The parade starts. The time caption comes first, then the felt signals of music, lights and the distant door breathing, then the procession begins to move with Vesper and Kandra in it.

Fans behind the rope line shout his nicknames. His flame tries to surge on its own; he counts inwardly and forces it back down, repeating to himself that he is scenery. The cause (flame rising) must be read before the suppression captions.
The procession halts at the C-zone selfie stop. A young woman at the front of the crowd holds her phone out with both hands and asks politely for a photo.
Vesper looks down at the phone and wonders what it captures, recalling the tale of a shadow-taking mirror. Then courtesy settles it: refusing would be rude.

Vesper accepts, bows with a mimed hat-doff and leans toward the phone. He tints his flame slightly whiter, and the phone screen shows a soft glow where his face would be, with brass seams and the dark below his collar washed to white.
The woman gushes over the result. The praise lands on his lamp glass and his flame brightens one step, undoing a little of his restraint.

facts.statement: It is 8:20. Vesper cannot read human clocks, but his body knows the moment: music rises underfoot, the lights come on all at once, and somewhere at the far end of the route the door takes a deep breath.
The parade procession starts moving.
Unnamed fans shout to Vesper using two affectionate nicknames, asking him to look their way.

The cheering washes against his lamp glass and his flame tries to rise by itself. Vesper counts inwardly and presses it back down, reminding himself that he is background, a prop, and that streetlamps do not speak.
On entering the C zone the music slows and the procession stops. It is the selfie zone.
The young woman at the front holds out a black flat device (a phone) with both hands and politely asks to take one photo together.

Vesper looks down at the device. Yesterday he went through this ritual twenty-some times. Humans say they 'capture' something with it, and he wonders what is captured. An old tale from beyond the door tells of a mirror that takes away shadows, and this might be something of that kind.
Because a lady asked politely, and refusing a request would be rude, he decides to accept.

Vesper says it is an honor, bows at the waist with a gesture as if doffing a hat, and leans in. The device comes right up to his lamp glass. He shifts his flame color very slightly whiter; on the screen, soft light spreads over the place where his face would be and washes out the brass seams and the empty darkness below his neck.
The woman praises the light-bleed mood as being just like a movie. The praise taps his lamp glass and his flame brightens by one step.

brief.style: Full-color Korean romance-fantasy comedy webtoon, clean expressive linework, soft cel shading, warm night palette; flame glow as key light and emotion cue; large crisp Korean lettering.

moments.action: Night theme-park parade route: parade lights snap on all at once; tall lamp-headed Vesper stands poised at the start, Kandra's candle head nearby among human gothic-costumed performers.
The procession walks forward; ordinary fans behind the rope line wave phones and shout toward Vesper.
Close on Vesper's cracked glass lamp head as cheers wash over it: his flame leaps upward on its own.
Vesper stands rigid and composed like scenery, his flame pressed back down small inside the glass.
Procession halted at the selfie stop; a young woman at the front of the crowd holds a black phone out to Vesper with both hands.
Vesper's lamp head tilts down toward the black phone in the woman's hands, his tall figure still.
Vesper bows, leaning in, white glove raised as if doffing a hat; flame faintly whiter; the phone at his lamp glass shows a soft white glow where his face would be.
The young woman beams at her phone screen in delight while beside her Vesper's flame glows one step brighter.

units.text: 베스퍼는 당황했다. 그리고 두 번째 사람이 판을 내밀었을 때, 이상한 점을 깨달았다.
아무것도 빠져나가지 않았다.
오히려 무언가가 들어왔다.
"목소리 너무 좋으세요."
한 단계.
"허리 숙이는 거 봐, 신사야 진짜."
또 한 단계. 의식 하나를 치를 때마다 가스통에 기름을 붓는 것처럼 속이 차올랐다.
그는 추론을 고쳤다. 이 의식은 빼앗는 쪽이 아니었다. 채우는 쪽이었다.
그래서 더 곤란했다.
"하트 해 주세요, 하트!"
베스퍼는 그 말을 몰랐다. 곁에 있던 꼬마가 엄지와 검지를 겹쳐 보여 주었다. 그는 흰 장갑 낀 손가락으로 그 모양을 한 치의 오차도 없이 따라 했다. 손가락 끝의 각도까지 맞췄다.
비명이 터졌다. 좋은 쪽으로.
불꽃이 황금색으로 번쩍 솟았다. 베스퍼는 황급히 그것을 눌렀다. 누른 자리에서 빛이 옆으로 튀었고, 가장 가까이 있던 판에 새하얀 줄이 그어졌다. 빛을 고르게 틀던 손이 어긋난 것이었다.
"삼 분이요! 신사님, 삼 분 됐어요!"
인파 너머에서 다온의 목소리가 날아왔다. 베스퍼는 마지막 판을 향해 깊이 고개를 숙이고 몸을 돌렸다. 등갓 안이 뜨거웠다. 누른 불이 빠져나갈 데를 찾지 못한 채 유리 안쪽을 핥고 있었다.

plan.intent: At the selfie stop, Vesper finds that his assumption was wrong. He had braced for the phone to take something from him, but with the second request he realizes that each small ritual feeds him instead. Each compliment raises his flame one step, like fuel poured into a tank. That makes it harder to hide, not easier. The comedy builds as he earnestly copies a finger heart shown by a child, down to the exact angle of the fingertips. The crowd's delighted scream then pushes his flame into a golden flare. When he hurriedly presses it down, the light spills sideways and leaves a white streak on the nearest phone: the first visible mistake of his concealment. Daon calls time from beyond the crowd, and he bows and turns away. His flame is still trapped and burning hot inside the glass. The reader should leave with a mix of warmth and pressure: being loved is filling him up, and there is nowhere safe for it to go.
plan.staging:
Setting: continuous with the previous scene. The procession is halted at the C-zone selfie stop of the fictional park's night parade. Fans with phones crowd behind a barrier. There is no readable signage, logo, festival title, or on-screen UI text anywhere.

NON-HUMAN COUNT: Vesper is the only gas-lamp-headed figure in the scene. Kandra is not in this excerpt; if she appears at all, she is the only candle-headed figure, stays in the background, and does not act or speak. Every fan, child, performer, and staff member is an ordinary human with a normal human head.

Vesper: very tall and slender, towering over the crowd. His head is a brass-framed glass gas lamp with one living flame and a thin crack at the upper left of the glass. He wears a dark high-collared tailcoat and white gloves, with empty darkness below the collar. There is no face, eye, mouth, or smile mark on the lamp; emotion reads only through flame color, brightness, and posture.

Flame progression, all relative, in this order:
- Beat-2: one step brighter after text-4, then one more step after text-6.
- Beat-5: a golden flare, then visibly pressed back down.
- Beat-6: the flame looks contained, but heat and motion are pressed against the inside of the glass, as if licking the inner surface.
Do not add other color meanings. The gas-tank comparison in ch-1-p-46 is a metaphor only; never draw a tank, canister, or oil.

The finger heart: an unnamed human child near the barrier shows a crossed thumb-and-index finger heart. Vesper copies it with one white-gloved hand, stiffly exact, matching the fingertip angle. The contrast between the casual child gesture and his precise imitation is the comic beat. The child has no lines.

The white streak: when he presses the golden flare down, the light jumps sideways, and a single pure white line appears on the phone nearest to him. Keep this one clear, small, readable mark tied visually to the sideways spill of light. It is not an explosion and does not damage anything else.

Speakers:
- text-4, text-6, and text-10 are spoken by unnamed human fans. Each is a spoken balloon with a tail to a fan, never a caption box. They may be different fans; tails decide who speaks.
- text-14 is Daon (c3), calling from beyond the crowd. She may be small or partly hidden behind heads, holding her radio, or only her balloon tail may come from off-panel toward the crowd's far side. Keep her identity (black half-up bob, staff jacket) if she is shown.
- Vesper speaks no line in this scene.

Required order:
1. text-1 through text-3.
2. text-4, then text-5, then text-6, then text-7.
3. text-8 and text-9.
4. text-10, then text-11 attached to the child's demonstration.
5. text-12 with the crowd's delighted reaction, then text-13 with the press-down and the white streak.
6. text-14, then the deep bow to the last phone and the turn away, with text-15 last.

LETTERING: previous attempts misspelled look-alike syllables. Copy every text id character for character, including quotation marks, commas, and periods. Pay special attention to:
- the doubled-consonant syllables in text-2 and text-15;
- the final syllables of text-9 and text-13;
- the honorific ending in text-4.
Never substitute a visually similar syllable. Never write speaker names or labels in balloons.

Panel count, sizes, cameras, and which beats share a panel are left to the artist.
uncertainties: ch-1-p-43 praises his voice, implying Vesper spoke during an earlier photo, but his words are not given. Do not add a line for him.

Whether the compliments in ch-1-p-43, ch-1-p-45, and ch-1-p-49 come from the second fan, the child's companions, or different people is unstated. They are unnamed humans, not Woo Taerim (c4); the speaker field reads narrator only because of the host constraint.

ch-1-p-52 says a white line was drawn on the nearest phone but does not state whether it is on the screen, in the captured photo, or on the device surface. It is also unstated whether its owner notices it. Show it as a light mark associated with the phone; do not depict any reaction to it.
The source does not say whether anyone besides Vesper notices the golden flare as unusual. The scream is described as delight, so do not draw alarm.
The child's relation to the fan who asked for a heart is unstated.
Daon's exact position and whether she is visible are unstated; only that her voice comes from beyond the crowd. Do not show her doing anything else.
The number of photos taken before the last phone is unstated. Do not show a count or a timer.
The exact color after the flame is pressed down, and in the final beat, is unstated. Only the heat and the trapped, licking motion inside the glass are fixed.
Kandra is not mentioned in ch-1-p-40 through ch-1-p-54, and her presence or actions here are unknown.

beats.action: Still flustered from the first photo, Vesper faces a second fan's phone and realizes that nothing is being taken from him. Something is coming in instead.
Fan compliments land in succession, first on his voice and then on his gentlemanly bow. With each one his flame climbs a step, filling like a tank.
Vesper corrects his theory: the ritual fills rather than steals. The correction makes his problem worse, because hiding just got harder.
A fan asks for a heart. Vesper does not understand. A child beside the barrier shows a finger heart, and Vesper replicates it with exact precision in his white gloves.
The crowd shrieks happily. His flame spikes golden, and he rushes to press it down. The light jerks sideways and leaves a stark white streak on the nearest phone.
Daon's time call cuts through the crowd. Vesper bows deeply to the final phone and turns away, the pent-up fire still licking the inside of his glass.

facts.statement: Vesper is flustered. When a second person holds out a phone for a photo, he notices something strange.
Nothing drains out of him during the ritual. Instead, something flows in.
Unnamed fans praise his voice and then the way he bows like a true gentleman. Each compliment fills him one more step. The source compares it to pouring oil into a gas tank, one ritual at a time.
Vesper revises his reasoning: the ritual does not take, it fills. This makes his situation more difficult.

A fan asks him to make a heart. Vesper does not know the term. A child nearby demonstrates by crossing thumb and index finger, and Vesper copies the shape exactly with his white-gloved fingers, matching even the angle of the fingertips.
The crowd screams in delight.

His flame flares golden. He hurriedly presses it down. At the pressed spot the light jumps sideways, and a pure white line appears on the nearest phone. The hand that had been tuning his light evenly slipped.
Daon's voice carries from beyond the crowd, announcing that the three minutes are up. Vesper bows deeply toward the last phone and turns away.
Inside his lamp shade it is hot. The suppressed fire has nowhere to escape and licks the inner surface of the glass.

moments.action: A second fan behind the barrier holds out her phone to towering Vesper, who looks down at it with startled, flustered posture, his lamp flame steady.
A smiling fan gushes up at Vesper beside the raised phone; his lamp flame glows one step brighter.
Vesper bows low at the waist toward the phone while another fan points at him in delight; his flame burns one more step brighter.
Vesper stands rigid amid the cheerful crowd, shoulders tense, his noticeably brighter flame filling the glass.
A fan calls out eagerly; a small human child beside Vesper casually shows a thumb-and-index finger heart as Vesper bends down, studying it intently.
Vesper holds up one white-gloved hand in a stiffly exact finger heart matching the child's angle, while fans behind the barrier scream with joy.
Vesper's golden flare is squashed low inside his glass; one thin ray of light spills sideways, leaving a single small pure-white streak on the nearest phone.
Daon calls from beyond the crowd, small behind heads; Vesper turns away from the last phone, his contained flame pressed hot against the inner glass.

units.text: 광장에 이르자 조명이 한 점으로 모였다.
칸드라와 함께하는 순서였다. 안무 표에는 '볼 뽀뽀'라고 적혀 있었다. 촛불 아가씨가 발끝을 들고 가로등 신사의 등갓에 입을 맞추는 시늉을 하면, 신사가 불빛으로 답하는 장면이었다. 어제 이 장면에서 관객석이 무너질 듯 들썩였다고 했다.
칸드라가 다가왔다. 발끝이 들렸다. 초 꼭대기의 불꽃이 그의 유리에 닿을 듯 말 듯 가까워졌다.
그 순간 그녀의 불꽃이 옆으로 눕는 것이 보였다. 촛농 한 방울이 흘러내려 그의 장갑 위에 떨어졌다.
베스퍼의 불이 튀었다.
청백색으로 한 번, 황금색으로 한 번. 다시 청백색. 등갓이 제멋대로 깜빡였다. 광장이 함성으로 뒤집혔다.
"연출 미쳤다, 불 깜빡이는 거 봐!"
칸드라는 이미 한 발 물러나 관객에게 손을 흔들고 있었다. 누워 있던 불꽃이 다시 곧게 서 있었다. 베스퍼는 묻지 않았다. 불을 낮추고 그녀 곁에 섰다. 장갑 위의 촛농은 아직 따뜻했다.

plan.intent: A choreographed pretend kiss, the crowd-pleaser from the night before, becomes a private moment the audience cannot read. The reader should feel the lights narrow onto the two lamp-headed performers. Then, in the closest instant, Kandra's flame tips sideways and a single drop of wax lands on Vesper's glove. Vesper's own fire jumps and he loses control of his color, flickering between blue-white and gold. That flicker betrays both alarm and something warmer, and the plaza roars, taking it as a brilliant effect. The comedy of the misread cheer sits on top of a quiet sting. Kandra has already stepped back, waving, her flame upright again as if nothing happened. Vesper does not ask. He lowers his light and simply stands beside her, and the scene closes on the one piece of evidence that it did happen: the wax on his glove is still warm. The reader leaves with warmth that has a cost underneath it, and a question he chose not to voice.
plan.staging:
Setting: the plaza on the parade route of the fictional park, at night, during the 8:20 PM parade. This picks up after the C-zone selfie stop from the previous scene. Parade lighting converges on one spot where Vesper and Kandra perform. An audience of ordinary humans surrounds the plaza, many holding phones. There is no readable signage, logo, festival title, or on-screen UI text anywhere. The choreography sheet named in text-2 exists only as narration and does not need to be drawn.

NON-HUMAN COUNT: Exactly two non-human figures appear.
- Vesper (c1) is the only gas-lamp-headed figure. He is about 2 m tall and slender. His head is a brass-framed glass gas lamp with one living flame and a thin crack at the upper left of the glass. He wears a dark high-collared tailcoat and white gloves, with empty darkness below the collar.
- Kandra (c2) is the only candle-headed figure. Her head is a thick ivory pillar candle with a flame on top and hardened wax drips down its sides. She is about 175 cm tall, noticeably shorter than Vesper, and wears a dark Victorian gown.
- Neither has a face, eyes, mouth, or expression marks. Emotion reads only through flame shape, color, brightness, and posture.
- Every audience member, staff member, and other performer is an ordinary human with a normal human head.

Necessary spatial facts:
- Because of their height difference, Kandra rises on tiptoe to bring her candle flame near his lamp glass.
- The flame comes very close to the glass without clearly touching it, and it is this closeness that must read.
- The wax drop falls onto one of Vesper's white gloves. The source does not say where his hand is, so place the glove wherever the drop can fall onto it naturally, and keep the drop small and legible against the white glove.

Flame states, in this order:
1. Kandra's flame tips sideways, which signals anxiety.
2. Vesper's flame jumps.
3. Vesper's lamp flickers blue-white, then gold, then blue-white.
4. Kandra's flame stands straight again while she waves.

plan.intent: After the loud warmth of the kiss number, the scene narrows into Vesper's private watch as the procession passes the door. The reader should feel two tempos at once: the parade keeps moving to its music, and underneath it Vesper keeps a centuries-old count. His flame leans toward the door on its own. He keeps walking and counts the floor lights as they come on beneath the procession. The fourth light is late by half a beat. No human could catch the gap, but he does, and the silence that follows is the tension. He does not turn his head. Only his flame leans a little further. Nothing visibly crosses out of the dark, and the next light comes on exactly on time. The scene ends on that ordinary, correct beat, which reads less like relief than like an unanswered question. The reader should leave unsure whether the delay was a glitch or a sign, and aware that Vesper alone noticed it.

IDENTITY: Vesper (c1) is the only gas-lamp-headed figure. He is a very tall, slender gentleman whose head is a brass-framed glass gas lamp with one living flame and a thin crack at the upper left of the glass. units.text: 퍼레이드가 끝났을 때 베스퍼의 머리는 끓는 주전자 같았다.
유리 등갓이 손을 댈 수 없을 만큼 달아올랐다. 눌러 둔 빛과 쏟아진 칭찬과 튀어 버린 불꽃이 한데 엉켜 안에서 웅웅 울렸다. 생각이 흐릿했다. 이대로 천막에 들어가면 누군가는 그의 머리가 인형탈답지 않게 뜨겁다는 걸 눈치챌 것이다.
그는 천막 뒤편, 장비 케이스가 벽처럼 쌓인 구석으로 들어갔다. 조명 받침대와 둘둘 말린 전선 사이였다. 칸드라는 보이지 않았다. 사람도 없었다.
베스퍼는 등갓 꼭대기의 작은 황동 뚜껑에 손을 얹었다. 굴뚝 캡이었다. 문 너머에서는 굳이 열 일이 없던 것이었다.
그가 뚜껑을 비틀어 열었다.
회색 연기가 한꺼번에 솟았다. 뭉게뭉게, 제법 성대하게 피어올랐다. 속이 가벼워졌다. 불꽃이 비로소 제 크기로 숨을 쉬었다. 그는 눈을 감는 대신 불빛을 가늘게 낮추고 긴 숨을 한 번 더 내쉬었다.

plan.intent: The parade is over, and the warmth the reader just shared with the crowd has become Vesper's private problem. He is overheated: suppressed light, the flood of praise and a stray spark are all trapped inside his glass. The reader should feel the pressure of a body that cannot pass as a costume much longer, then his quiet choice to hide rather than enter the tent. The mood tightens as he slips into a walled-off, empty corner and checks that no one, not even Kandra, can see him. It releases with gentle comedy when he twists open a small cap he never needed back home and a grand, slightly absurd plume of grey smoke rolls out. The scene ends small and relieved. His flame breathes at its proper size, and he dims it to a thin glow and lets out one more long breath. It is a private maintenance ritual the reader alone witnesses.
plan.staging:
Setting: the same fictional park on parade night, just after the 8:20 PM parade has finished. The scene moves from near the backstage waiting tent to a dark corner behind it. Keep everything free of signage, logos, festival titles, labels on the cases and UI text.

IDENTITY: Vesper (c1) is the only figure who must appear. He is a very tall, slender gentleman whose head is a brass-framed glass gas lamp with one living flame and a thin crack at the upper left of the glass. He wears a dark high-collared tailcoat and white gloves, with empty darkness below the collar. He has no face, eyes or mouth. His state reads only through flame size, brightness and posture. The small brass chimney cap sits at the very top of the lamp, matching his reference. Kandra (c2), Daon (c3) and Taerim (c4) do not appear. The source says Kandra is not in sight, so do not draw her anywhere, even in the background. If any humans are visible near the tent at the start, they are ordinary people with normal heads who do not react to him. From the corner onward, nobody else is present.

Necessary spatial facts:
- The corner is behind the tent. Equipment cases are stacked high enough to form a wall-like barrier, with light stands and coiled cables around it. It is empty and hidden.
- The overheated state before the cap opens may be shown with heat shimmer, a cramped, swollen-looking flame and an inner glow in the glass. The kettle comparison in text-1 is narration, so do not draw a literal kettle. Do not show smoke until the cap is opened.
- The source says the shade is too hot to touch, but it does not say whether he flinches, uses his gloves for protection or is hurt. Draw no reaction to the heat.
- He rests one gloved hand on the cap first (text-8), then twists it open (text-10). Whether the cap is fully removed or only swung open is not stated. Either reads acceptably as long as it clearly opens.
- Grey smoke rises from the chimney opening all at once, in a big billowing plume. Gentle comedy is welcome. The smoke only rises from the chimney; the source does not say anyone outside the corner sees it.
- Afterward, the flame settles to a natural, relaxed size, then is lowered to a thin, dim glow. The source states no flame color, so do not introduce a specific color shift.
- He has no eyes or mouth. Do not draw eyelids, a mouth or a face to show him closing his eyes or breathing. Convey the long exhale through posture (shoulders dropping) and perhaps a last faint wisp from the chimney.

LETTERING (blocking fixes from the previous render): every caption is narration in a caption box with no speaker label. Keep text-1 through text-15 in order and copy each one character for character from texts[].text. Two captions were misspelled last time and must be checked glyph by glyph. In text-6, the word before the verb meaning 'stacked' is the simile meaning 'like a wall'. Its first syllable is the one used for 'wall', not a similar-looking syllable. In text-8, the final verb means 'rested/placed (a hand) on'. It must not be rendered as the unrelated word meaning 'did not exist'. Give both captions enough box space and a large, clean font so every syllable block is legible.

The artist chooses the panel count, sizes, framing and how captions are grouped. Prefer fewer, larger panels, and give the smoke release room to land.
uncertainties: The source does not say how Vesper touches a cap on a shade described as too hot to touch (ch-1-p-71, ch-1-p-73). It is unstated whether the gloves protect him or the cap is cooler. Draw no explanation.

The meaning of ch-1-p-73's remark that there was no reason to open the cap beyond the door is unexplained. It may be that he never overheated there, or that praise and suppression are new to him. Do not visualize a cause.
Whether the cap is fully removed or hinged open is not stated (ch-1-p-74).
The phrases about closing eyes and breathing in ch-1-p-75 are figurative for a being without eyes or a mouth. How the exhale looks physically is unstated.
Vesper's flame color during this scene is not stated, so no color code is applied.
Whether anyone outside the corner can see or smell the smoke is not stated.
The kettle image in ch-1-p-70 is a narrator simile. Whether steam or sound actually leaks before the cap opens is not stated.
The source does not say where Kandra is, only that she is not in sight (ch-1-p-72).

beats.action: The parade has ended. Vesper is overheated: the glass shade is too hot to touch, and the held-down light, the praise and the flared flame hum together inside. His thoughts blur.
He realizes that walking into the tent like this would let someone notice his head is too hot for a costume, so he does not go in.
He slips behind the tent into a corner walled off by stacked equipment cases, among light stands and coiled cables, and finds it empty. No Kandra, no people.
He rests a gloved hand on the small brass chimney cap at the top of his shade, a part he never needed to open back home, and twists it open.
Grey smoke gushes up in a big, almost ceremonious billow. The pressure inside eases and the flame settles to its proper size.
Rather than closing eyes he does not have, he narrows his light to a thin, low glow and exhales one more long breath, alone in the corner.

facts.statement: When the parade ended, Vesper's head was like a boiling kettle.
His glass lamp shade had grown too hot to touch.
The light he had held down, the praise poured on him and the flame that had flared were tangled together and humming inside.
His thoughts were hazy.
If he entered the tent in this state, someone would notice his head was hotter than a costume head should be.
He went into a corner behind the tent where equipment cases were stacked up like a wall, between light stands and coiled cables.
Kandra was not in sight, and there was nobody else there either.
Vesper placed his hand on the small brass cap at the very top of his lamp shade. It was a chimney cap.
On the other side of the door, he had never had any particular reason to open it.
He twisted the cap open.
Grey smoke rose all at once, billowing up in a fairly grand plume.
He felt lighter inside, and his flame finally breathed at its proper size.
Instead of closing his eyes, he lowered his light to a thin glow and let out one more long breath.

Vesper alone in a dim corner behind the tent, walled in by stacked equipment cases among light stands and coiled cables; nobody else anywhere in view.
Vesper's white-gloved hand rests on the small brass chimney cap at the very top of his glowing lamp head.
Chimney cap twisted open, a big, grand billow of grey smoke rolls up from the opening atop Vesper's lamp head, gently comic.
Vesper alone in the corner, shoulders dropped in relief, his flame lowered to a thin, dim glow, a faint wisp curling from the open chimney.

plan.intent: The relief of the previous scene turns into discovery. The reader first only hears a voice: someone has come looking for a burning smell, and the footsteps stop at the corner of the case wall. The reveal lands in three quick visual notes (half-up hair, the mole at the end of the right eyebrow, a red extinguisher held in both hands with the pin half pulled) before the name confirms it: it is Han Daon, and she came ready to put out a fire, not to find a creature. Her round eyes climb the way a reader's would: up to the glass shade, past the open chimney cap, up the still-billowing smoke, then back down to the empty space above the collar where a head should be. Vesper's answer is the only one he has, and it is comic and a little sad at once: he freezes completely, like a street lamp, betting that human eyes will read him as a lighting prop propped in the corner. The joke is that the smoke will not freeze with him. Her trembling call breaks the spell, and his flame flinches on its own, which betrays him because his light cannot hide feeling. The scene ends on a held standoff between a human with an extinguisher and a smoking gas lamp among the equipment, with the slow closing music drifting in from beyond the tent. The reader should laugh at the failed disguise and feel the weight of the moment: someone has now seen him.
plan.staging:
Setting continues directly from the previous finished scene: same night, same dark corner behind the backstage tent, walled in by stacked equipment cases, with light stands and coiled cables. Lit mainly by Vesper's own lamp; the tent is nearby but its interior is not the stage here. No signage, logos, festival titles, name tags or UI text anywhere; the extinguisher carries no printed words.

IDENTITY: Vesper (c1) is the only lamp-headed figure: very tall, slender, brass-framed glass gas-lamp head with one living flame and a thin crack at the upper left of the glass, small brass chimney cap at the very top, dark high-collared tailcoat, white gloves, empty darkness below the collar. No face, eyes or mouth. Han Daon (c3): small young woman, shoulder-length black bob tied half-up, round dark-brown eyes, tiny mole at the end of her RIGHT eyebrow, staff jacket and radio. Kandra (c2) and Taerim (c4) do not appear. No other people are in the corner.

Necessary spatial and continuity facts:
- The chimney cap is OPEN throughout this scene (ch-1-p-80 names it open). Grey smoke keeps rising from the top opening in every moment of the scene; it never stops (text-12). Smoke comes only from that top opening.
- Daon arrives at the corner of the case wall (text-2). text-1 may be placed as an off-panel or edge-of-panel balloon before she is fully seen; its tail points toward where she enters.
- Daon holds a red fire extinguisher in both hands with the safety pin pulled about halfway out. She does NOT spray it at any point; the source only shows her holding it ready.
- Her eyeline in text-6/text-7 travels up the shade, past the open cap and smoke, then settles on the empty darkness above his collar. The artist may show this as one gaze or several; the endpoint must be the empty collar.
- The freeze (text-8 to text-12): Vesper goes perfectly still, standing in the corner like a prop lamp; his flame is motionless, no flicker. Do not change his flame color or brightness during the freeze; the source states only that breath and trembling stop. The comic contrast is the still body under a smoke plume that keeps billowing.
- text-13 is Daon's line; draw her balloon with a slightly shaky outline to carry her trembling voice (ch-1-p-85). Right after, his flame gives a small involuntary start (text-15). No color code is stated, so show only a jump or wobble of the flame.
- Final standoff (text-16 to text-18): the two face each other among the equipment piles, neither moving, extinguisher still in her hands, smoke still rising. The closing music is only a caption; do not draw musical notes with text or any speaker labels.

Text kinds: text-1 and text-13 are Daon's speech balloons (tails to Daon, never to Vesper). All other texts are narration captions. Vesper has no lines in this scene. Keep texts in id order text-1 through text-18 and copy each character for character, including ellipsis characters, commas and periods. Never write speaker names inside balloons or captions.

Panel count, sizes, cameras, caption grouping and reveal pacing are the artist's choice. The standoff may take a large closing panel.
uncertainties: ch-1-p-76 does not name its speaker. Attributing text-1 to Daon (c3) is an inference from the footsteps stopping and her reveal right after; it is not stated outright.
Who told Daon about the burning smell (the reported-speech ending of ch-1-p-76) is not stated. Do not show another informant.
The distance between Daon and Vesper and whether she steps any closer after stopping are not stated.
What Daon concludes from the empty space above the collar is not stated. She may or may not already suspect he is not a costume; draw her reaction as fear or tension without a stated conclusion.
Whether Daon recognizes him as the parade's lamp gentleman at this moment is not stated.
Vesper's flame color and brightness during the freeze and the flinch are not given in this excerpt; only stillness and then an involuntary start are stated.
Whether the freeze actually fools her at any point is not stated; the narration only says how he should look to human eyes, and the unstopped smoke undercuts it.
Whether Daon later uses the extinguisher is not stated in this excerpt; she only holds it with the pin half pulled.
The exact source of the closing music and how far it carries are not stated beyond 'beyond the tent'.

beats.action: While Vesper stands in the corner with his cap open and smoke rising, a voice approaches asking about a burning smell, and the footsteps halt at the corner of the case wall.
The newcomer is revealed piece by piece: half-up hair, the eyebrow mole, a red extinguisher gripped in both hands with its pin half pulled. It is Han Daon, armed for a fire.
Daon's gaze climbs the glass shade, the open chimney cap and the rising smoke, then drops and stops at the empty darkness above his collar.
Vesper freezes totally, flame dead still like a street lamp, trying to pass as a corner lighting prop. The smoke keeps billowing from his open cap regardless, undoing the disguise.
Daon speaks to him in a shaky voice. Her address breaks his freeze, and his flame gives an involuntary start.
Standoff: extinguisher-holding human and smoking gas lamp face each other among the equipment, both motionless, while slow closing music drifts in from beyond the tent.

facts.statement: A voice says that people reportedly smell something burning here. The line is heard before the speaker is shown.
Footsteps stop at the corner of the wall of stacked cases.
The arrival has half-up hair, a small mole at the end of the right eyebrow, and holds a red fire extinguisher in both hands with its safety pin pulled halfway out.
The arrival is Han Daon (c3).
Her round eyes rise to Vesper's glass shade, pass the open chimney cap, follow the smoke that is still billowing up, and then stop at the empty place above his collar where something should be.
Vesper does the only thing he can: he freezes completely, stopping both his breath and the trembling of his light, as a street lamp would be still.
The narration states that to human eyes he should now look like a lighting prop left standing in the corner.
Only the smoke does not stop.
Daon calls out a hesitant excuse-me, and her voice trembles.
The moment she speaks to him, his freeze breaks, and his flame flinches by itself.
The human holding the extinguisher and the smoke-puffing gas lamp face each other among the piles of equipment. Neither moves.
Beyond the tent, closing-time music is slowly playing.

Han Daon stops at the case-wall corner: half-up black bob, tiny mole at her right eyebrow's end, both hands gripping a red fire extinguisher with its safety pin pulled halfway out.
Daon's round eyes fix on the empty darkness above Vesper's collar, his glowing glass lamp head and billowing smoke plume above it.
Vesper stands rigidly still in the corner like a street lamp, his flame perfectly steady inside the glass, smoke rising from his open cap.
Motionless Vesper looks like a lighting prop left among light stands and cables, while grey smoke keeps billowing up from his open chimney cap.
Daon calls out in a shaky-outlined speech balloon, extinguisher still in both hands; inside Vesper's glass, his flame gives a small involuntary jump.

device.summary: 베스퍼의 불빛이 이 화의 칸 테두리와 여백 색, 칸의 밝기를 정합니다. 평온할 때는 호박색, 당황하면 분홍, 문에서 멀어져 꺼져 갈 때는 차가운 파랑으로 테두리가 바뀌고 칸이 어두워지며, 불빛이 돌아오면 칸도 하나씩 밝아집니다. 이야기 내용은 원작 그대로이고 보여 주는 방식만 바꿨습니다.
device.hint: 이 화는 베스퍼의 불빛이 페이지의 조명입니다. 칸 테두리와 그림 뒤 빛의 색이 그의 불꽃을 따라 바뀝니다.

units.text: 연기가 굴뚝 캡 위에서 한 가닥 비틀리며 흩어졌다.
베스퍼는 그 연기가 천막 지붕 쪽으로 올라가는 것을 끝까지 좇았다. 눈이 어디에 있느냐고 인간이 묻는다면 설명하기 곤란했지만, 어쨌든 그는 보았다. 소화기를 든 인간의 시선이 연기와 그의 목깃 사이를 오가는 것도 보았다. 위, 아래. 위, 아래.
"드라이아이스죠?"
인간이 먼저 말했다. 목소리가 갈라져 있었다.
"아니, 내장 팬. 팬이죠? 탈 안에 쿨링 팬 들어가잖아요. 그쵸? 그리고 목은, 목은 그거죠, 검정 천. 암막. 조명 때문에 안 보이는 거. 특수효과죠? 특수효과 맞죠?"
한 호흡에 질문이 세 번이었다. 베스퍼는 그 수를 셌다. 이 인간은 같은 질문을 세 번 던지고, 세 번 모두 '그렇소'라는 답을 받고 싶어 했다.
쉬운 일이었다. 한마디면 끝났다. 요즘 탈은 다 이 정도로 뜨겁소. 혀끝에 이미 그 문장이 걸려 있었다.
그는 장갑 낀 손가락으로 굴뚝 캡을 딸깍 닫았다. 연미복 옷깃을 한 번 바로잡았다. 그리고 모자를 벗어 드는 신사처럼 등갓째로 머리를 깊이 숙였다.
"놀라게 해 드려 송구하오, 숙녀분."
불빛이 숙인 각도를 따라 바닥의 케이블 뭉치 위로 둥글게 번졌다.
"허나 이것은 장치가 아니오. 내 머리요."
인간의 입이 벌어졌다. 닫히지 않았다.

plan.intent: The reader watches a frightened human staffer beg for a comfortable explanation of the smoke and the empty collar. Vesper holds a ready-made lie on his tongue, then chooses courtesy and truth. Comedy comes from her frantic triple-checking against his unhurried gentleman ritual, and the scene lands on the flat reveal and her frozen, open mouth. Tension is the gap between the easy lie and the honest bow.
plan.staging: Setting: dark corner behind the backstage tent among equipment cases, with a bundle of cables on the floor and the tent roof above. Two figures only: Vesper (c1), about 2m tall, brass-framed glass gas-lamp head with a thin crack on the upper left of the glass, a small chimney cap on top, dark high-collared tailcoat, white gloves, empty darkness above the collar; and the human staffer (read as Han Daon, c3), much shorter, clearly half-up tied shoulder-length black bob, round dark-brown eyes, tiny mole at the right eyebrow tip, staff jacket and radio, holding a fire extinguisher throughout. Height difference means her eyes travel upward to the smoke and down to his collar. His lamp is the key light; when he bows, the lamp tilts toward the floor and its light pools on the cables. The chimney cap is open while smoke rises and closed after the click. Vesper has no mouth: his balloons point to the glass lamp; text-6 is an unspoken thought and must not look like speech. Lettering note from review: text-10 and text-11 are two separate balloons (or clearly separate lines) so the period after the first sentence is kept exactly; never join them with a comma. Page device: steady calm amber glowing borders fit this scene, since the source reports no change in his flame here. Panel count, sizes and cameras are the artist's choice.
uncertainties: The source calls her only 'the human'; identification as Han Daon (c3) comes from the direction and story spine, not from this excerpt.
Source does not state any change of Vesper's flame color or brightness during this scene; do not invent flashing, pink blinking or dimming beyond steady light.
Whether the smoke is still rising when she starts talking, or has already dispersed, is not stated.
How Vesper sees without eyes is deliberately unexplained; do not draw eyes or a face on the lamp.
Whether she ever aimed or used the fire extinguisher is not stated; she only holds it.
Exact distance between them and her position relative to the cable bundle are unspecified.

beats.action: Smoke curls up from the chimney cap toward the tent roof; the extinguisher-holding human's eyes flick between the smoke and Vesper's empty collar, up and down, repeatedly.
She breaks the silence first with a cracked-voice guess.
She piles on fan and blackout-cloth explanations, pleading for confirmation; Vesper silently tallies three questions in one breath.
Vesper holds the easy lie ready but unspoken; the moment of temptation.
Decision made: he clicks the cap shut, straightens his collar, and folds into a deep gentleman's bow with the whole lamp.
Bowed, he apologizes; his lamplight pools round over the floor cables.
He states the plain truth in two short sentences; her jaw drops and stays open.

facts.statement: A single twisting strand of smoke rises above the chimney cap on top of Vesper's lamp head and disperses.

Vesper follows the smoke with his sight until it reaches the tent roof, though he has no visible eyes. The human holding a fire extinguisher keeps looking back and forth between the smoke and his collar.

The human speaks first, in a cracked voice, offering dry ice, then an internal cooling fan, then black blackout cloth hidden by lighting as explanations, and asks each time for confirmation that it is a special effect.
Vesper counts three questions in one breath and understands she wants a yes to all three.
An easy lie is already on the tip of his tongue, but he does not say it aloud.
With a gloved finger he clicks the chimney cap shut, straightens his tailcoat collar once, and bows deeply with the whole lamp shade, like a gentleman lifting his hat.
He apologizes to her as a lady. As he bows, his light follows the angle of the bow and spreads in a round pool over the bundle of cables on the floor.
He states that this is not a device but his head. Her mouth falls open and does not close.

Vesper bows deeply like a gentleman, whole lamp tilted toward the floor, amber light pooling round over the cable bundle; Daon watches, extinguisher in hand.

units.text: 다음 순간 그녀는 소화기를 앞으로 쭉 내밀었다. 두 팔을 곧게 뻗은, 거의 무언가를 바치는 자세였다. 빨간 몸통이 등불 아래서 반짝였다.
베스퍼는 그것을 내려다보았다. 붉은 원통. 검은 뿔 같은 관. 손잡이 아래 반쯤 뽑힌 은색 고리.
처음 마주한 이에게, 몸을 굽혀, 붉은 것을 두 손으로 내민다.
문 너머에도 비슷한 예법이 있었다. 겨울의 첫 방문객에게 불씨 담은 등잔을 건네는 일. 인간의 방식은 조금 더 무겁고 조금 더 차가울 뿐이었다.
그는 두 손을 가지런히 모아 소화기를 받쳐 들었다. 그리고 한 번 더 허리를 숙였다.
"과분한 환대요. 이 세계에서 받은 첫 선물이니 소중히 간직하겠소."
머리의 가스등이 발그레한 분홍으로 두 번 깜빡였다.
인간은 빈손을 내려다보았다. 빈손을 한 번, 베스퍼를 한 번.
"아니, 그게, 저 지금 뿌리려고……."

plan.intent: A comedy of crossed etiquette. The frightened staffer thrusts the fire extinguisher forward to use it. Vesper reads the gesture through the customs he knows and receives it as a formal welcome gift. The reader sees the half-pulled pin and knows what she meant long before he does. The main laugh comes when his solemn thanks meets her blank, empty hands. The warmth rests on his sincerity: he is honoring a custom that was never offered. His flame stays steady amber until his thanks, then blinks a blush pink twice. That one change is the scene's emotional leak and its page-color cue.
plan.staging:
Continuous from the previous scene, in the same dark corner behind the backstage tent among equipment cases and floor cables. Vesper's lamp is the key light. Two figures only.

Vesper (c1): about 2m tall, brass-framed glass gas-lamp head with a thin crack at the upper left of the glass, small chimney cap already closed, dark high-collared tailcoat, white gloves, empty darkness above the collar. There is no face, eyes or mouth anywhere, including inside the flame; do not repeat the smiling-face-in-flame drift noted in the previous review.

The human staffer (Han Daon, c3): much shorter, with a half-up shoulder-length black bob, round dark-brown eyes, a tiny mole at the right eyebrow tip, staff jacket and radio.

Necessary spatial facts:
1. She starts holding the extinguisher and extends it toward him with both arms straight. Because of the height gap, he looks down at it.
2. The extinguisher is red with a black hose. Its silver pin stays visibly half pulled out under the handle in every view. Nothing is sprayed at any point.
3. After the handover, he holds it with both gloved hands together, supporting it from below, and bows again. Her hands are then empty.
4. The pink blinks happen after his thank-you line (text-5) and before her reply (text-6).

Balloon rules: Vesper has no mouth, so text-5 points to the glass lamp head. The captions for beat-3 are interior narration. Do not illustrate the world beyond the door, the winter visitor or the ember lamp as a flashback.

Text-1 and text-2 both come from Vesper's viewpoint, but they are captions, not thought balloons.

Page device: glowing borders are steady calm amber through beat-5. They turn blush pink for the blink beat. The artist decides how the pink persists or fades over the final beats; the source only states two blinks. Brightness stays normal throughout, because the source states no dimming here.

Panel count, sizes, cameras and the grouping of beats into panels are the artist's choice.
uncertainties: Unit ch-2-p-15 says the offerer bends the body. Unit ch-2-p-13 only states straight extended arms and an offering-like posture. It is unclear whether she actually leans or bends, or whether Vesper reads it that way. A slight forward lean is compatible; a deep bow is not stated.
What she intended to spray at (the earlier smoke, Vesper's head, or something else) is not stated in this excerpt.
Whether she lets go willingly or he simply takes it from her extended hands is not specified. The source says only that he holds it in both hands and that her hands end up empty.
This excerpt refers to her only as 'the human'. Her identification as Han Daon (c3) comes from the previous scene and the foundation.
How long the pink color lasts after the two blinks, and what color his flame shows afterward, are not stated.
The source does not describe her facial expression during the final line beyond her gaze moving between her empty hands and Vesper.
Whether Vesper notices the half-pulled pin as dangerous is not stated. He lists it only as a feature of the object.

beats.action: She abruptly shoves the extinguisher out at arm's length toward Vesper. She means to use it, but her rigid, outstretched pose reads like an offering. The red body catches his lamplight.

Vesper looks down from his height and inventories the object piece by piece. The half-pulled silver ring is the detail the reader should catch as a sign of imminent spraying. Vesper does not treat it that way.

Misreading takes hold. He maps her gesture onto the winter-visitor custom from beyond the door and concludes the human version is simply heavier and colder. This is interior narration only, with no depicted scenery from beyond the door.
He accepts the extinguisher reverently in both gloved hands, cradling it from below. He bows once more, and the extinguisher passes from her grip into his.
Formally and warmly, he thanks her for the gift.
His flame gives him away: two rosy pink blinks, the first change in his light in this scene.
She gives a blank one-word response. Her gaze drops to her now-empty hands, then rises to Vesper.
She starts to protest that she was about to spray it, and the words trail off unfinished. He is still holding the 'gift'.

facts.statement: In the next moment she thrusts the fire extinguisher straight forward. Both arms are fully extended, in a posture that looks almost like presenting an offering. The extinguisher's red body gleams under the lamplight.
Vesper looks down at the extinguisher and registers three things: a red cylinder, a black horn-like hose, and a silver ring half pulled out beneath the handle.
Vesper reads the gesture as someone meeting him for the first time, bending the body and holding out a red object with both hands.
Beyond the door there was a similar custom: handing the first visitor of winter a lamp holding an ember. To him, the human way seems only a little heavier and a little colder.
He brings both hands neatly together and holds the extinguisher supported from below. Then he bows at the waist once more.
He thanks her for an undeserved welcome. He calls it the first gift he has received in this world and says he will treasure it.
The gas lamp that serves as his head blinks a rosy blush pink twice.
The human answers with a stunned one-word question. She looks down at her empty hands, then at Vesper, once each.
She stammers the start of an explanation: she was about to spray it just now. The line trails off unfinished.

units.text: 말끝이 흐려질 때, 그녀의 허리춤에서 무전기가 치직 울렸다.
[다온 쌤, 아까 천막 뒤 탄내 신고 건. 확인됐어요?]
인간의 손이 무전기로 갔다. 엄지가 송신 버튼 위에 올라갔다. 베스퍼는 그 엄지를 지켜보았다. 눌리지 않았다. 한 박자. 두 박자. 퍼레이드 북소리였다면 벌써 다음 소절로 넘어갔을 시간이었다.
"……확인 중이에요. 잠시만요."
엄지가 떨어졌다. 그녀가 숨을 크게 들이쉬었다.
"좋아요. 좋아. 일단은 사람이 다쳤을 수도 있는 거니까."
그녀는 자기 자신에게 하듯 말했다.
"머리에서 연기가 났어요. 그건 어떤 경우든 이상한 거예요. 그쵸? 의무실 가요. 사무동에 있어요. 거기 선생님이 보시면—"
"숙녀분, 나는—"
"한다온이요. 이름. 명찰 있잖아요."
그녀가 가슴께를 톡 쳤다.
"가요. 지금 21시 14분이니까 마감 전엔 도착해요."
그녀가 연미복 소매를 잡아끌었다. 베스퍼는 끌려갔다. 분부를 거스르는 것은 예법에 어긋났다. 적어도 그는 그렇게 믿었다.

plan.intent: A small workplace choice made under pressure. A colleague on the radio asks Daon a direct question about the burning-smell report behind the tent. The honest answer would expose the creature standing in front of her. The reader should feel the held breath of her hesitation, told through her thumb resting on the transmit button and not pressing. She stalls, then steadies herself aloud. She settles on the one frame that lets her act without deciding anything yet: someone might be hurt, so go to the infirmary. Vesper's attempt to speak is cut off. She hands him her name instead, and he gives in to being towed off by the sleeve out of the etiquette he believes in. The comedy comes from his dignified surrender to what he reads as a lady's command. The weight comes from her pause: the first time she withholds a report.
plan.staging:
This scene continues directly from the previous one, in the same dark corner behind the backstage tent among equipment cases and floor cables. Vesper's lamp is the key light. Two figures are on-panel. The radio caller is never shown.

Revision fix: the earlier caption that named the protagonist was misrendered twice. That sentence of unit ch-2-p-25 is now carried visually instead of lettered. Show Vesper's lamp head tilted down toward her thumb, clearly attending to it, and letter only text-3 beside that moment. No caption or balloon in this scene contains the protagonist's name. Do not add it back anywhere.

Identity:
- Vesper (c1): about 2m tall. His head is a brass-framed glass gas lamp with a thin crack at the upper left of the glass. He wears a dark high-collared tailcoat and white gloves, with empty darkness above the collar. There is no face, eyes or mouth anywhere, including inside the flame.
- Han Daon (c3): much shorter. She has a half-up shoulder-length black bob, round dark-brown eyes and a tiny mole at the tip of her right eyebrow. She wears a staff jacket with a radio at her waist.
- Continuity: at the end of the previous scene Vesper was holding the red fire extinguisher with its pin half pulled, and her hands were empty. This excerpt does not mention the extinguisher again. It may stay in his hands as continuity, but nothing is sprayed and it must not become a focus.

Necessary spatial facts:
1. The radio is at her waist. Her hand moves to it, and her thumb rests on the transmit button through beat-2.
2. The thumb comes off the button only after text-5 (unit ch-2-p-27).
3. Text-1 and text-2 come from the radio. The balloon tail points to the radio, since the speaker is an unnamed off-panel colleague. Use a radio-style (jagged or electronic) balloon.
4. For text-11 she taps her own chest where the name tag is. Draw the name tag blank, with no lettering.
5. At the end she grips his tailcoat sleeve and pulls, and he follows. The direction of travel is toward the staff-only area. Where exactly the scene ends (still backstage or entering the grey corridor) is open.

Balloon rules:
- Vesper has no mouth, so text-10 points to his glass lamp head.
- Text-7 and text-13 are narration captions, not thought balloons.
- Text-10 and text-9 are both cut off with a dash. His line interrupts hers, and her text-11 interrupts his.

Page device: glowing borders and gutters stay calm amber throughout. This excerpt states no change in his flame and no dimming, so keep panel brightness normal. Do not start the distance-dimming progression here.

Panel count, sizes, cameras and the grouping of beats into panels are the artist's choice.
uncertainties: Unit ch-2-p-25 states the thumb was not pressed for two beats. Whether she presses it to speak text-5 is not stated; unit ch-2-p-27 only says the thumb comes off afterward. Leave the moment of transmitting ambiguous rather than drawing a clear press.
It is not stated whether the caller hears text-5 or whether the radio replies again. No further radio text should be added.
Her facial expression during the pause is not described beyond the big breath in unit ch-2-p-27.
Whether Vesper still holds the extinguisher from the previous scene is not stated in this excerpt; it is continuity only.
What Vesper intended to say after text-10 is unknown.
The source does not say whether his flame changes color or brightness during this exchange, so no change is specified.
The destination is the infirmary in the office building. How far they get within this scene and whether they reach the staff corridor are not stated.
The radio speaker's identity is not given beyond using her team nickname.

beats.action: Her trailing-off protest from the previous scene is cut by the radio crackling at her waist. The colleague's question lands: has the burning-smell report behind the tent been confirmed? The report is about the very being in front of her.
Her hand goes to the radio and her thumb hovers on the transmit button without pressing. Vesper, looking down, fixes his attention on that thumb. Time stretches over two unanswered beats.
She stalls the caller with a non-answer. Then the thumb lifts off the button and she draws a big breath. The report is withheld, not falsified.

She talks herself into a course of action, half to herself and half to him. Someone might be hurt, smoke from a head is strange no matter what, so it is the infirmary in the office building. She is mid-plan when he interrupts.
Vesper starts a formal objection. She cuts him off by giving her name, pointing to her name tag, and tapping her chest once.

She states the time as a deadline, grabs his tailcoat sleeve and tows him off. The very tall figure follows the much shorter one without resisting, because in his understanding a command from her is not to be defied.

facts.statement: As her previous words trail off, the radio at her waist crackles.
An off-panel colleague addresses her by her team nickname. They ask whether the earlier report of a burning smell behind the tent has been confirmed.

Her hand goes to the radio and her thumb rests on the transmit button. Vesper watches the thumb. It is not pressed for two beats, which the narration measures against a parade drum that would already have moved to the next bar.
She answers that she is still checking and asks the caller to wait a moment.
Her thumb comes off the button and she takes a big breath.
She says, as if to herself, that it is fine for now because someone might have been hurt.

She reasons that smoke came from his head, which is strange in any case. She tells him to go to the infirmary in the office building, where the staff there can look at him. She is cut off mid-sentence.
Vesper begins to object, addressing her formally as a lady. She interrupts with her name, Han Daon, points out her name tag, and taps her chest once.
She tells him to come. She states that it is now 21:14, so they will arrive before closing.
She pulls him by the tailcoat sleeve and he lets himself be pulled. He does so because defying a command breaks etiquette, or at least he believes so.

brief.style: Full-color Korean romance-fantasy comedy webtoon, clean expressive linework, soft cel shading, warm night palette lit by Vesper's lamp; thin calm-amber glowing panel borders and gutters, normal brightness.

moments.action: Behind the backstage tent, the radio at Daon's waist crackles with an off-panel colleague's question in a jagged radio balloon tailed to the radio; tall lamp-headed Vesper stands before her.
Daon's thumb rests on the radio's transmit button, unpressed, while Vesper's glass lamp head tilts down toward that thumb, attentive; two narration captions hold the stretched pause.
Daon, thumb still resting on the transmit button, murmurs a hesitant stalling reply toward the radio at her waist.
Daon's thumb lifts off the button; she draws a big breath and steadies herself, speaking as if to herself, with a narration caption.
Daon looks up at Vesper's lamp head, reasoning aloud about the smoke from his head and urging him to the infirmary; her second line ends at a dash.
Vesper's formal objection, tailed to his glass lamp head, breaks off as Daon taps her own chest at a blank name tag, giving her name.
Daon grips Vesper's tailcoat sleeve and tows him off toward the infirmary, stating the time; the tall gentleman follows with dignified compliance, with a narration caption.

review.evidence: Seven panels: the radio crackles with the colleague's question (1); her thumb on the button with Vesper watching and the two beat captions (2); her stall (3); her self-steadying line and the caption that she spoke as if to herself (4); the smoke and infirmary lines (5); Vesper's objection cut off by her name as she taps her blank name tag (6); she tows him by the sleeve into the fluorescent staff corridor as she states the time (7). Borders and gutters glow steady amber. All thirteen lines match the source.

units.text: 천막 뒤편을 벗어나 직원 통로로 들어섰다. 형광등이 길게 이어진 회색 복도였다. 벽에는 코팅된 점검표가 붙어 있었고, 누군가 그 아래에 '간식 서랍 비었음 ㅠ'라고 적어 두었다.
열 걸음쯤 걸었을 때 베스퍼는 알아차렸다. 그의 불빛이 제 구두 코를 비추지 못하고 있었다.
스무 걸음. 등갓 안의 불꽃이 심지 끝으로 오그라들었다. 가스 냄새가 옅어졌다. 등 뒤에서 무언가가 실처럼 그를 당겼다. 수백 번의 겨울 동안 한 번도 끊어져 본 적 없는 실이었다.
"다온 님."
"네, 거의 다 왔어요. 저기서 꺾으면—"
돌아가 주시오.
그 말이 목구멍 어딘가까지 올라왔다. 그에게 목구멍이라 부를 만한 것이 있다면.
그는 말하지 않았다. 지금은 분부를 받는 중이었다. 이 인간은 그를 걱정해서 이리로 데려가고 있었다. 걱정받는 도중에 되돌아가자고 청하는 것은—
"……길이, 퍽 어둡소."
"네? 불 다 켜져 있는데요."
그녀가 돌아보았다. 그리고 멈췄다.
