plan.intent: A quiet horror inside a comedy of manners. Vesper follows Daon into the grey staff corridor because she is taking him to the infirmary out of concern. With every step away from the gate, his flame shrinks and something behind him pulls like a thread. The reader should feel the light drain out of the page while the fluorescent tubes stay on. His plea to turn back rises and stops before it is spoken, because etiquette forbids refusing a command given in kindness. He does not say he is fading. He only understates that the way is rather dark. She answers literally, since every light is on. The humor sits in that gap: his politeness against her practical reply. The weight arrives when she turns, looks at him and stops. The page ends on what she sees, without saying what she thinks.
plan.staging:
Continuity: this picks up right after the previous scene, which ended with Daon towing Vesper by the tailcoat sleeve toward the staff area. Setting: grey staff-only corridor, long white fluorescent tubes, all switched on and drawn on in every panel. Only two figures appear: Daon (c3) and Vesper (c1).

Identity:
- Vesper: about 2m, brass-framed glass gas-lamp head with a thin crack at the upper left of the glass, dark high-collared tailcoat, white gloves, empty darkness above the collar. No face, eyes or mouth anywhere, including inside the flame.
- Daon: much shorter, half-up shoulder-length black bob, round dark-brown eyes, tiny mole at the tip of her right eyebrow, staff jacket, radio at her waist.
- Extinguisher: carrying the extinguisher from the earlier scene is optional continuity only. This excerpt does not mention it. It must never be used or become a focus.

Necessary spatial facts:
1. Daon walks ahead and Vesper follows behind her, in the same direction, deeper into the corridor. The pull he feels (text-6, text-7) comes from behind him, toward where they came from. Show it only as posture or a slight lean backward. Do not draw a literal visible thread or any creature.
2. The laminated checklist on the wall has blank or unreadable lines. The only legible writing is the handwritten note text-1, placed just below the checklist.
3. For text-3, his shoe toes sit in shadow even though the ceiling tubes are lit.
4. For text-5, the flame inside the glass is visibly reduced to a small point at the wick tip.
5. During text-8 and text-9 she is still facing forward or glancing sideways while gesturing toward a turn ahead. She does not look directly at his lamp until the final beat.
6. For text-19 she has turned fully around toward him and is stopped mid-step. What exactly she sees is left to the image: at minimum his tiny flame in the glass.

Balloons:
- Vesper has no mouth, so text-8 and text-17 point their tails to his glass lamp head.
- Text-10 is a thought balloon with trailing circles toward his lamp. It is never spoken aloud.
- Text-9 ends in a dash because it is cut off. Text-16 is a narration caption that also ends in a dash.
- All other narration lines are captions, not thought balloons.

Lettering accuracy (revision fix): in the previous image, the first word of the ch-2-p-43 closing sentence was misrendered. That sentence is now split into four short captions, text-13 to text-16. Give text-16 its own caption box, with large clear type and generous spacing. The first two syllables of text-16 must be exactly the same glyph pair as the verb stem inside text-15, which directly precedes it. Letter them identically, and do not substitute a similar-looking syllable. Every caption must match its texts[].text character for character. Keep all balloons and captions white with dark text, fully legible even in the darkest panel.

Page device (presentation only):
- Glowing borders and gutters start calm amber at the corridor entrance.
- From text-2 onward, each step dims the panels and desaturates them, while the borders thin and cool.
- The darkest point falls around beat-5 or beat-6: an almost-black panel with one tiny cold-blue flame dot and the white captions.
- Beat-7 and beat-8 stay dark and cold.
- His light does not come back in this excerpt, so do not restore brightness or warm colors anywhere.

Panel count, sizes, cameras, and how beats are grouped into panels are the artist's choice.
uncertainties: Who wrote the snack-drawer note (text-1) is not stated; it is attributed to narrator as ambient physical text.
The source gives a thinning gas smell (ch-2-p-38) that cannot be lettered or drawn directly; how, or whether, to suggest it visually is open.
The thread-like pull in ch-2-p-38 is a sensation; the source does not say it is visible, so no literal thread or entity should be drawn.
The source states the flame shrinks but not that it changes color; the cold-blue tint is the page-design device and the genre code for fading, not a stated story event.
What Daon sees when she turns (ch-2-p-46) and what she feels or does next are not described.
Whether Daon can perceive his dimming at all before she turns is not stated; her reply in ch-2-p-45 suggests she has not yet noticed.
The end of the ch-2-p-43 reasoning is cut off; what he would have concluded is unknown.
Whether Vesper still carries the extinguisher from the earlier scene is not stated in this excerpt.
How far along the corridor they are when she stops, and where the turn she mentions lies, are not specified.

beats.action: Daon leads Vesper out from behind the tent into the grey staff corridor under long fluorescent tubes. On the wall is a laminated checklist with a small handwritten note stuck below it, an everyday detail of staff life. This is the last moment of normal light.
About ten steps in, Vesper notices that the pool of his own light no longer reaches the toes of his shoes. The first dimming happens quietly, noticed only by him.

At twenty steps the flame in his lamp shrinks down to the wick tip and the gas smell thins. Something behind him tugs like an old, never-broken thread, pulling back toward where they came from. The page keeps darkening.
He calls her name. She answers brightly without stopping, already indicating the turn ahead, and her sentence is cut off.
The plea to turn back rises inside him and gets no further than his nonexistent throat. It stays unspoken.
He swallows the plea out of etiquette. She is worried about him, and he is under her orders, so asking to go back feels improper. His reasoning breaks off unfinished. He is at his dimmest here.
All he lets out is a polite understatement that the way is rather dark. She replies literally, puzzled, because every tube overhead is lit. The comic gap between them is at its widest.
She turns back to look at him and freezes. The scene ends on her stopping. Her reaction beyond that is not given.

facts.statement: They leave the back of the tent and enter the staff passage. It is a grey corridor lined with long fluorescent tubes. A laminated checklist is posted on the wall, and under it someone has written a note that the snack drawer is empty.
After about ten steps Vesper notices that his light no longer reaches the toes of his own shoes.

At twenty steps the flame inside the lamp glass shrinks toward the tip of the wick. The gas smell grows faint. Something behind him pulls at him like a thread that has never once broken in hundreds of winters.
Vesper calls Daon by name. She replies that they are almost there and starts to say that they turn over there, but she is cut off.
The words asking her to go back rise to somewhere in his throat, if he can be said to have one. They are not spoken.

He does not say it. He considers himself to be under orders. This human is taking him here because she is worried about him, and he feels that asking to turn back while being worried over would be improper. The sentence breaks off before he finishes the thought.
Instead he says hesitantly that the way is rather dark. She answers in confusion that all the lights are on.
She turns to look back at him, and then she stops.

plan.intent: This scene continues directly from Daon turning around and freezing. The reader first sees what she saw: Vesper's light has collapsed to almost nothing, and his body gives out. Then the scene reverses. A small human hand, stronger than it looks, catches him before he reaches the floor. Daon babbles in panic but does not wait for an explanation. She shoulders him, grabs the rolled-away extinguisher, and turns back the way they came. She chose that direction out of instinct and has no idea it was the right one. Only Vesper knows, because the pull behind him eases the moment she turns. The payoff is quiet and counted: one step, then two, and his light creeps back until it reaches only as far as her sneaker laces. The warmth is earned by her doing more than her share without asking. The page starts at its darkest and brightens panel by panel, but not all the way back.

beats.action: Opening on what Daon turned to see. His flame is a single blue pinpoint, dimmer than a match. His legs forget their weight, his knees fold and the extinguisher slides from his arms. The corridor tubes are still on.
Mid-fall, before he reaches the floor, a small hand clamps onto his arm and holds. The grip is surprisingly strong.
Daon's panicked, stammering outburst while she holds him up. It is comedic in rhythm, but she is genuinely frightened.

She acts without waiting for any reply. She hauls his arm over her shoulder, scoops up the rolled extinguisher one-handed and pivots back toward where they came from, the tent side. Vesper says nothing.
Dramatic irony. She does not know why that direction; he does. The instant she turns, the pull that had been dragging at him from behind slackens.
Counted recovery as they walk back. On the first step the blue dot swells slightly. On the second step it bleeds into yellow.

They push through the door at the corridor's end into the quiet maintenance area beside the empty parade route. His returned light is just enough to reach the laces of her sneakers. This is a modest recovery, not a full blaze. The scene ends here.

facts.statement: Vesper's head is now dimmer than a single match. A single blue dot flickers inside the glass.
His legs lose their strength and his knees buckle. The fire extinguisher he was holding against his body slips out of his arms.
Before he hits the floor, something grips his arm. It is a small hand, and it is stronger than expected.
Daon cries out in confusion and alarm, calling to him and asking what is happening. The unit has no dialogue tag; the speaker is the human who caught him, Daon.
Daon does not wait for an answer. She puts his arm over her shoulder and picks up the extinguisher, which had rolled away, with one hand. She turns back the way they came, toward the tent.
The narration says she probably did not know why she chose that direction, but Vesper did. As soon as she turned around, the thread loosened.
After one step the blue dot grows slightly. After two steps it spreads into yellow.
They push through the door at the end of the corridor and step out into the maintenance area beside the parade route. By then his light has returned enough to illuminate the laces of Daon's sneakers.

인간은 휴대폰을 꺼냈다. 화면 불빛이 그녀의 얼굴을 파랗게 물들였다. 엄지가 빠르게 움직였다. 베스퍼는 등갓을 기울여 화면을 들여다보았다.
[머리에서 불나는 사람]

plan.intent: This is a quiet breather right after the corridor collapse. It turns from grave to gently comic without losing the weight underneath. Daon and Vesper sit in the empty maintenance area. Neither has recovered, and one of them does not really breathe at all. When she asks her low question, Vesper has a clear chance to lie again. He tilts his lamp head down and tells the truth instead: distance from his post dims him, and the distance they just covered was nearly the end. He does not answer her echo of that word. His flame answers for him, cooling blue and slowly returning to yellow. Daon falls back on the only tool she has and searches her phone. Vesper leans in to watch. The results are uselessly human: scalp heat, herbal tea. His dignified question about the black slab gets a flat verdict, and then a hair-loss shampoo ad. The final beat belongs to his misreading. He does not know the word, but from her face he concludes, with relief, that it is a calamity that does not concern lamp-folk. The warmth sits on top of an admission he has just made. The page stays mostly calm and warm, with one cold dip.

beats.action: Establish the hush right after the doorway. The covered parade vehicle is asleep in the maintenance area, and a distant cleaning cart crawls along the empty route. The only other light nearby is Vesper's modest flame, continuing from the previous scene.
Daon sets Vesper down on an equipment case and flops down beside him. Both are spent and simply breathe for a while. Her chest heaves; his collar-darkness has nothing that breathes.
Daon breaks the silence first, quietly. This is a low, careful question, not panic.
Vesper has the option to lie again and does not take it. He dips his lamp head slightly and states the truth plainly, ending on how close to the end he just came.
The last word is echoed back as a question. Vesper stays silent, and his flame answers instead: it cools to blue, then slowly warms back to yellow. This is the one cold dip in the scene.
Daon pulls out her phone. The screen glow paints her face blue, and her thumb types fast. Vesper leans his lamp head over to peer at the screen, where her query sits in the search field.
Results pour down the screen: scalp-heat coping tips and hot-headed tea. They are earnest, human and useless.
Vesper asks, with formal hope, whether the black slab knows his condition. Daon flatly concludes that it knows nothing at all.
She kills the screen, which goes dark, and deadpans the final insult: a hair-loss shampoo ad appeared.
Comic button from Vesper's side. He does not know the word, reads her face and concludes, relieved, that this disaster does not concern his kind. The scene ends here.

facts.statement: The maintenance area is quiet. A single parade vehicle sits under a cover, described as sleeping. Far off, a cleaning cart moves slowly along the parade route.

The human (Daon, continuing from the previous scene) sits Vesper down on an equipment case and then drops down heavily beside him. For a while both of them only breathe. The narration notes that what one of them does can barely be called breathing.
The human speaks first, in a low voice, asking whether he goes out when he gets far away.
The narration states that he could have lied this time too. Instead, Vesper lowers his lamp head slightly.
Vesper confirms it. If he moves away from the place where he is supposed to stand, his fire dies down. At the distance they reached a moment ago, it is almost the end.
The word for the end is repeated back as a question. Vesper does not answer. His light cools to blue, then slowly turns yellow again.
The human takes out her phone. Its screen light tints her face blue, and her thumb moves quickly. Vesper tilts his lamp head to look at the screen.

The search query appears on the screen (ch-2-p-63). A string of results follows, including an article about five ways to cope when stress heats the scalp and one about teas for people whose heads run hot.
Vesper asks whether the black slab knows about his situation too. The reply is that it does not know; it knows nothing at all.
The human turns the screen off and reports that a hair-loss shampoo ad came up.
Vesper does not know what the hair-loss word means. Judging from the human's expression as she says it, he concludes that it is, fortunately, a calamity unrelated to lamp-folk.

units.text: 무전기가 다시 울렸다.
[다온 쌤? 탄내 건. 보고 올려야 돼요.]
인간은 무전기를 들었다. 엄지가 버튼 위에서 멈췄다. 베스퍼는 이번에도 박자를 셌다. 하나. 둘. 셋.
그녀의 눈이 그에게 왔다. 등갓, 목깃, 품에 돌아온 소화기. 그리고 복도 쪽, 그가 꺼질 뻔한 거리를 한 번 쟀다.
넷에서 엄지가 눌렸다.
"아…… 네. 소품 조명 과열이요. 가로등 탈. 전원 내리고 식혔어요. 자체 해결 완료했습니다."
[오케이. 수고.]
치직. 끝이었다.
인간은 무전기를 허리춤에 걸었다. 그리고 두 손으로 얼굴을 덮었다.
"망했다."
"무엇이 망하였소?"
"저 방금 허위 보고 했어요. 기록 남아요. 21시 23분. 소품 조명 과열. 자체 해결."
손가락 사이로 목소리가 새어 나왔다.
"이제 내일 제가 '사실 그 탈 안에 아무도 없어요' 하면, 그럼 어제는 왜 해결 완료라고 했냐, 그러겠죠. 그쵸?"
베스퍼는 그 말의 절반을 이해했다. 나머지 절반은 짐작했다. 그녀가 방금 그를 위해 무언가를 내려놓았다는 것.

plan.intent: This scene is a small, quiet sacrifice that plays as office-comedy despair. The radio breaks the breather in the maintenance area: a colleague wants the burning-smell incident reported. Daon holds the radio with her thumb frozen on the button. Vesper silently counts the beats, as he did before. In that pause she looks him over (lamp shade, collar, the extinguisher in his arms) and then measures the corridor distance where he nearly went out. That look is her motivation. On the fourth beat she presses and files a false report with brisk competence. The reply is two words and a click. Only after the line goes dead does the cost land. She hangs up the radio, buries her face in her hands and explains, in timestamps, exactly why she is doomed. Vesper understands half of it, guesses the other half, and grasps that she just gave something up for him. The reader should laugh at her professional panic and feel the weight under it: the cover-up has become a permanent log entry in her name.
plan.staging:
Continuity: the scene continues directly from the previous scene, in the same quiet parade maintenance area beside the empty route at night. The covered parade vehicle and the equipment cases are there. Vesper (c1) and Han Daon (c3) are still seated side by side where the phone scene ended. Only these two are visible. The colleague exists only as a voice from the radio.

Identity:
- Vesper is about 2m tall. His head is a brass-framed glass gas lamp with a thin crack at the upper left of the glass. He wears a dark high-collared tailcoat and white gloves, with empty darkness at the collar. He has no face, eyes or mouth.
- Daon is small, with a half-up shoulder-length black bob, round dark-brown eyes and a tiny mole at the tip of her right eyebrow. She wears a staff jacket and carries a handheld radio.

Necessary spatial facts:
1. Daon holds the radio up for beats 1 to 5. Her thumb is visibly paused over the talk button during the counting pause, and it presses on the fourth beat.
2. The corridor they came from is visible or implied in her line of sight during beat-3. It is the grey staff corridor with fluorescent tubes. Her glance goes from Vesper toward it.
3. The fire extinguisher is in Vesper's arms (see uncertainties).
4. After the call ends, the radio hangs at her waistband. From beat-6 through beat-9 her face is covered by both hands, and her lines are spoken through her fingers.
5. Vesper's flame state is not described in this excerpt. Keep it steady at the calm amber level carried over from the previous scene. Do not add pink blinking, smoke or color shifts. The glowing panel borders therefore stay a steady amber (presentation device only).

beats.action: The radio on Daon crackles again and cuts through the maintenance-area quiet. The unseen colleague asks for the burning-smell report.
Daon lifts the radio. Her thumb hovers, frozen, over the talk button. Vesper, beside her, silently counts the pause.
During the pause her gaze travels over Vesper (lamp shade, collar, the extinguisher in his arms). Then it goes once toward the corridor he nearly died down. This look is what decides her.
On the fourth beat she presses and delivers the false report in a smooth, professional voice.
The radio accepts the report in two words, crackles, and falls silent. The report is filed.
The composure drops. She clips the radio to her waistband, buries her face in both hands and pronounces her doom.
Vesper turns his lamp head toward her and asks, formally and sincerely, what exactly is ruined.
Still hidden behind her fingers, she lays out the logged false report in timestamp form. Her voice leaks out through her hands.
She plays tomorrow's interrogation forward: the truth now contradicts yesterday's record. She ends seeking confirmation she already knows the answer to.
Vesper's side closes the scene. He grasps half the words and guesses the rest: she has just laid something down for him. The scene ends on that realization, with no further action.

facts.statement: The radio sounds again. A colleague's voice addresses Daon by her team nickname and says the burning-smell incident must be reported upward.
The human (Daon) raises the radio. Her thumb stops above the button. Vesper counts beats again: one, two, three.
Her eyes come to him: his lamp shade, his collar, and the fire extinguisher that has returned to someone's arms. Then she measures once, toward the corridor, the distance at which he nearly went out.
On four her thumb presses the button. She reports that a prop light on the streetlamp costume overheated, that the power was cut and it was cooled down, and that the matter was resolved internally.
The radio answers with a short okay and thanks, then a crackle, and the exchange is over.
She hooks the radio onto her waistband, covers her face with both hands and says that she is done for.
Vesper asks, in his archaic register, what is done for.
Through her fingers she explains that she just made a false report, that it stays on record, and she recites its time and content.
She reasons that if she tells the truth tomorrow, she will be asked why she declared it resolved, and she ends by seeking confirmation.
Vesper understands half of what she said and guesses the other half: that she has just set something down for his sake.

plan.intent: A comic slip followed by a truce. Vesper answers Daon's sacrifice from the previous scene in the only way he knows: with ballroom formality. He rises and bows before an equipment case as if opening a dance, and pledges his debt. Mid-oath his own title escapes him (text-2). Daon catches the word at once (text-3). He stops cold, and the lamp betrays him with three fast flickers that no formality can hide. What follows is a small duel of repetitions: he insists it is nothing, she refuses to accept that, and he narrows the lie to tonight only. The reader should laugh at the grand bow undone by one careless noun, then feel the balance shift. Daon, who has just carried a false log entry for him, decides not to push. She states her shift times like a worker closing her shift, dusts herself off and turns the debt into a contract with conditions she withholds on purpose. He is the one left not knowing. The scene closes on her having the upper hand.

Identity:

He wears a dark high-collared tailcoat and white gloves, with empty darkness below the collar. He has no face, eyes or mouth. The phrase in ch-2-p-88 means he falls silent. Do not draw a mouth.

2. The triple flicker (text-3) happens right after text-2, while he is still in or just out of the bow. His posture stays composed and only the flame reacts.
3. Daon remains seated through text-7. She stands and brushes off her trousers only after that, then delivers text-8 on her feet.

beats.action: Vesper unfolds to his full height and makes a deep, courtly bow to the still-seated Daon, with a cluttered equipment case as his ballroom. He begins a solemn oath of debt and lets his title slip into it.
Daon seizes the stray word and throws it back as a question. The oath is interrupted.
Vesper freezes and says nothing, but his flame flickers rapidly three times. His body keeps its composure while his light gives him away.
A three-line stand-off. He denies it, she refuses the denial, and he retreats to a smaller claim: it is nothing only for tonight.
Daon holds a long look at him, then sighs and lets it go. She concedes in work-schedule terms, with a clock-out time and tomorrow's shift.
She stands, brushes off her trousers and turns the debt into a deal: they talk tomorrow, and she has conditions.
He formally asks what the conditions are. She flatly refuses to say until tomorrow. The scene ends on the withheld terms, with the formal gentleman left in suspense.

facts.statement: Vesper stands up and, in front of an equipment case, bows from the waist the way one gives the first greeting at a ball.
He tells Daon (addressing her with the honorific used in ch-2-p-86) that he owes her a great debt, and begins to swear by the name of the gatekeeper. He breaks off mid-sentence.
Daon repeats the word gatekeeper back to him as a question.
He falls silent. His light flickers quickly three times.
He says it is nothing. Daon says it does not seem like nothing. He answers that tonight it is nothing.
The human (Daon) looks at him for a long time, then sighs.
She agrees not to ask today. She states that she clocks out at 22:00 and is on the opening shift tomorrow.
She gets up and brushes off her trousers.
She says they will talk tomorrow and that she has conditions. He asks what the conditions are. She says she will tell him tomorrow.

units.text: 그녀가 손을 내밀었다.
"그리고 그거 주세요."
베스퍼는 품의 소화기를 내려다보았다. 그리고 조금 더 꼭 끌어안았다.
"선물을 되돌려 드리는 것은 무례요."
"선물 아니에요. 비품이에요. 소화기는 환영 선물이 아니라고요. 여기 관리 번호 붙어 있잖아요, 여기."
베스퍼는 붉은 몸통에 붙은 작은 스티커를 보았다. 숫자가 적혀 있었다. 인간 세계의 선물에는 번호가 붙는 모양이었다.
인간은 그를, 그리고 그의 머리를 보았다. 조금 전 푸르게 꺼져 가던 자리를.
"……아뇨, 그냥 갖고 있어요. 또 연기 나면 옆에 두는 게 낫겠다."
그녀가 등을 돌렸다.
"대신 잃어버리면 제 경위서예요. 제 경위서. 아시겠죠?"
"분부 받들겠소."
그녀는 직원 통로 문을 밀고 형광등 불빛 속으로 걸어 들어갔다. 한 번도 뒤돌아보지 않았다.
베스퍼는 소화기를 안고 그 자리에 서 있었다. 동선 쪽에서 청소 카트 바퀴 소리가 멀어졌다.
내일 그 인간은 조건을 들고 올 것이다. 무엇일지는 알 수 없었다. 다만 그가 이 자리를 떠날 수 없다는 사실을, 이제 이 세계에서 딱 한 사람이 알고 있었다.
머리의 불빛이 따뜻한 주황으로, 아주 조금, 오래 머물렀다.

plan.intent: A small tug-of-war over a red fire extinguisher turns into a quiet act of care. Daon holds out her hand to take back park equipment. Vesper clutches it tighter and refuses with courtly logic: returning a gift is rude. She corrects him in work terms. It is inventory, not a welcome present, and it has a management number. His grave misreading of the sticker lands as the scene's joke. Then Daon looks at his head, where his flame had been fading blue shortly before, and changes her mind. She lets him keep it in case he smokes again. She attaches the cost in her own currency: if it goes missing, she writes the incident report. He accepts the order with his usual formal word. She walks into the fluorescent staff corridor without looking back. He is left alone holding the extinguisher. The cleaning cart fades away, and the reader should feel that one person in this world now knows he cannot leave this spot. His flame settles into warm orange and stays there.
plan.staging:
Continuity: this follows directly from the previous finished scene, which ended with Daon refusing to state her conditions until tomorrow. It takes place in the same quiet parade maintenance area beside the empty route at night, with the equipment cases nearby and the staff corridor door within walking distance. Only Vesper (c1) and Han Daon (c3) are present. Daon is already standing after brushing off her trousers in the previous scene. Vesper holds the same red fire extinguisher in his arms from the start.

Identity:
- Vesper is about 2m tall and slender. His head is a brass-framed glass gas lamp with a living flame and a thin crack at the upper left of the glass. He wears a dark high-collared tailcoat and white gloves, with empty darkness below the collar. He has no face or mouth.
- Daon is small, with a half-up shoulder-length black bob, round dark-brown eyes and a tiny mole at the tip of her right eyebrow. She wears a staff jacket and has a radio at her waist.

Necessary spatial facts:
1. The extinguisher stays in Vesper's arms for the whole scene. It is never handed over.
2. The management-number sticker is small and sits on the red body of the extinguisher. It shows only illegible tiny marks. No readable digits or words.
3. When Daon looks at his head (ch-2-p-104), she is looking at his lamp. The blue fading happened earlier and is not happening now.
4. Daon turns her back (ch-2-p-106) before or while delivering text-6. Text-6 is spoken with her back turned or partly turned. Vesper answers text-7 to her back.
5. She exits through the staff corridor door into white fluorescent light and never looks back. Vesper does not follow. He stays where he is.
6. The cleaning cart is heard, not necessarily seen. It moves away along the parade-route side.

Flame and border device: through this excerpt Vesper stays near the door and does not move away, so do not apply the corridor darkening sequence to him. Keep calm amber panels and amber glowing borders. At the end, his flame and the panel borders shift to a faint, warm orange that lingers (ch-2-p-112, shown through color only, not lettered).

Lettering (critical revision fix):
- Copy every text character for character and letter each one exactly once.
- In text-6, the mark right after the first sentence is a PERIOD, not a comma. Break the balloon into three lines at the sentence ends so that line one ends with a clearly drawn period: line 1 is the first sentence ending in a period, line 2 is the two-word sentence ending in a period, line 3 is the question. Do not merge the first two sentences with a comma.

- Vesper's balloons (text-2, text-7) point to his glass lamp head. Daon's balloons (text-1, text-3, text-5, text-6) point to her.
- Text-4, text-8, text-9 and text-10 are white caption boxes with dark text and no tails.
- Ch-2-p-98, ch-2-p-100, ch-2-p-104, ch-2-p-106, ch-2-p-109 and ch-2-p-112 are shown through acting and color only, not lettered.

beats.action: Daon extends an open hand for the extinguisher. Vesper glances down at it and hugs it closer instead of giving it up.
Vesper refuses on grounds of etiquette, still hugging the extinguisher.
Daon rattles off the correction in staff terms and jabs a finger at the management-number sticker on the red body.
Vesper studies the tiny sticker with solemn attention and files away a wrong conclusion about human gifts. This is the comic payoff.
Daon's gaze moves from him up to his lamp head, where the flame had been fading blue shortly before. She relents and lets him keep the extinguisher as a precaution against more smoke.
She turns her back and lays down the cost: losing it means an incident report under her name. He accepts it as a command.
Daon pushes through the staff corridor door into white fluorescent light and does not look back.
Vesper remains alone in place, hugging the extinguisher, while a cleaning cart's wheels fade away along the route.

facts.statement: Daon holds out her hand and asks Vesper to hand over the item he is holding.
Vesper looks down at the fire extinguisher in his arms and hugs it a little tighter.
Vesper says that returning a gift is rude.
Daon says it is not a gift but park equipment, that an extinguisher is not a welcome present, and points out the management number attached to it.
Vesper looks at a small sticker on the red body of the extinguisher with a number written on it, and concludes that gifts in the human world come with numbers. The actual digits are not given.
Daon looks at him and at his head, at the place that had been fading blue a little earlier.
Daon reverses herself and tells him to just keep it, reasoning it is better to have it beside him if smoke comes out again.
Daon turns her back and warns that if he loses it, the incident report will be hers to write, asking whether he understands.
Vesper replies that he will obey her command.
Daon pushes open the staff corridor door and walks into the fluorescent light without looking back once.
Vesper stays standing in place holding the extinguisher. The sound of cleaning cart wheels recedes from the direction of the parade route.
Tomorrow Daon will come with conditions, unknown to him. Exactly one person in this world now knows that he cannot leave this spot.
The light of his head stays warm orange, only slightly, for a long time.

plan.intent: A hushed, slightly comic morning handshake between two new accomplices. The reader should feel the stillness of the park before opening, the oddness of a two-meter gas-lamp gentleman who has clutched a fire extinguisher all night, and the collision of two value systems: Daon's hurried, time-boxed workplace pragmatism (twenty minutes, one condition, a checkbox on a phone) against Vesper's archaic sense that any condition set is a solemn pledge that demands a seal. The humor comes from the mismatch in weight: she offers a to-do line, he receives an oath. The scene ends on Vesper's grave acceptance, leaving the coming formality as anticipation.
plan.staging: Setting is the maintenance area in daylight/early morning, before park lights are on; parade floats are under covers, and Vesper stands between them. Daon approaches from the passageway side, not from among the floats. Vesper is about two meters tall and Daon is in the low 160s cm, so the phone screen she offers must visibly reach Vesper's line of sight; whether she raises it high, he bends down, or both is left to the artist. Daon keeps the coffee in one hand while holding out the phone with the other. Vesper keeps holding the fire extinguisher; the source never says he puts it down. The phone screen's text line must be legible to the reader when shown. Vesper has no mouth, so his balloon tails point to his glass lamp head. No earpiece or radio transmission occurs in this excerpt, so no radio transmission bands are used. No other characters are present.
uncertainties: The line in ch-3-p-2 is spoken before Daon is described arriving; attribution to Daon (c3) is inferred from context and her following lines, and she may be heard before she is fully seen.
Why Vesper held the fire extinguisher all night is not stated in this excerpt; do not invent a reason or show him using it.
Vesper's flame color and brightness during the scene are not stated; any color cue is an artist choice and should not be presented as a specific source-given emotion.
Whether Daon's dark under-eyes come from lack of sleep, worry or something else is not stated.
The form of the formality Vesper announces in ch-3-p-11 (a seal or other ritual) is not shown in this excerpt; do not depict a seal being made.
Exact physical positions, distance between the two and whether Vesper stays bowed while reading are not specified.

beats.action: Quiet morning in the maintenance area: covered parade floats hunched like sleeping beasts, and Vesper standing among them still hugging the fire extinguisher he has held all night.
Daon's hedged greeting arrives as she strides in fast from the passageway, coffee in one hand, phone in the other, visibly short on sleep.
Vesper bows at the waist to her and acknowledges that she kept the appointment, treating it as a kept promise.
Daon deflates the ceremony: she was on the opening shift anyway, and she stresses a hard twenty-minute limit.
Daon thrusts her phone toward Vesper and announces a single condition; the screen's one unchecked line is revealed.
Vesper stares at the line for a long time; for him a condition is a stake and always carries a seal, so the casual checkbox takes on oath-like weight.
Vesper gravely accepts and announces he will observe formality befitting a solemn pledge, escalating her quick request into ceremony.

facts.statement: It is morning in the park before opening; the maintenance area is quiet, and parade floats sit crouched under covers.
Vesper stands among the covered floats holding a fire extinguisher in his arms and has not put it down once all night.
Daon walks in quickly from the passageway side, a convenience-store coffee in one hand and her phone in the other; the skin under her eyes is slightly dark.
Vesper bows at the waist and greets Daon, noting she came as promised.
Daon says she had to come anyway because she is on the opening shift, and that she has exactly twenty minutes, repeating the number.
Daon holds out her phone; the white screen shows a single black-text line with an empty checkbox, which she calls her one condition.
Vesper stares at the line for a long time; in his world, setting a condition means staking something (a name, fire, several winters), and a seal is always stamped on top.
Vesper accepts and declares that, since it is a solemn pledge, he will observe proper formality.

brief.style: Full-color Korean romance-fantasy comedy webtoon, clean expressive linework, soft cel shading; hushed early-morning maintenance area, pale daylight, Vesper's gas-lamp flame the warm accent.

moments.action: Quiet morning maintenance area: tarp-covered parade floats crouch like sleeping beasts, and tall lamp-headed Vesper stands among them hugging a red fire extinguisher to his chest.
Daon strides in from the passageway, convenience-store coffee in one hand, phone in the other, faint shadows under her eyes, calling out her greeting.
Vesper bows deeply at the waist, extinguisher still in his arms, while Daon, holding coffee and phone, answers him briskly.
Daon holds her phone up toward Vesper's lamp head, coffee in her other hand; the white screen shows one large, legible black line with an empty checkbox.
Close on Vesper's glass lamp head leaning toward the glowing phone screen, gazing at the single line in long, silent concentration.
Vesper straightens to full height, extinguisher hugged to his chest, grave and formal in acceptance, while small Daon looks up at him, coffee in hand.

units.text: 그는 소화기를 조심스레 내려놓고 왼손 장갑을 벗었다. 검지 끝에 굳은 촛농 한 점이 남아 있었다. 어젯밤 레이디의 불꽃에서 떨어진 것이었다. 베스퍼는 그것을 머리의 불꽃 가까이 가져갔다.
"잠깐만요. 뭐 하세요?"
"녹이는 중이오. 계약이란 본디 무언가를 녹여야 성립하는 법이니. 레이디의 촛농이 반쯤 녹으면 이 검은 판에 꾹 눌러……."
"아아아 안 돼요! 액정! 액정 녹아요! 이거 할부 아직 남았어요!"
다온이 휴대폰을 품에 끌어안고 두 걸음 물러났다. 베스퍼는 촛농을 든 채 굳었다. 불빛이 파르르 푸르게 식었다.
"……무례였소?"
"무례가 아니라 수리비요. 인장 같은 거 안 찍어도 돼요. 여기, 이 네모 칸 보이죠? 여기다 체크만 하시면 돼요. 손가락으로 쓱."
베스퍼는 네모 칸을 보았다. 작고, 비어 있고, 아직 누구의 것도 아닌 자리였다. 가문의 문장을 새길 자리 같았다. 그는 장갑을 다시 끼고 숨을 고른 뒤, 오른손 검지를 화면 위에 띄웠다.
"한 번에 그어야 하오? 두 번 그으면 서약이 두 배가 되오?"
"한 번이요. 그냥 한 번."
손끝이 화면에 닿았다. 아주 천천히, 모서리에서 모서리로 움직였다. 반듯한 체크 하나가 그어졌다. 다온이 들여다보더니 작게 중얼거렸다.
"……체크를 무슨 붓글씨처럼 쓰시네."
"이 몸이 처음으로 인간에게 거는 약조요. 비뚤 수는 없소."
말은 태연했다. 불빛은 분홍으로 두 번 깜빡였다. 인간에게 기대게 되었다는 사실이 어딘가 부끄러웠다. 그런데 그 부끄러움보다 조금 더 큰 무엇이 있었다. 베스퍼는 그것에 이름을 붙이지 않았다.

plan.intent: A small comic collision that turns into something tender. The reader should first feel alarm as Vesper, in complete earnest, begins a ritual from his world: melting Kandra's wax to stamp a seal onto what he calls the black plate. The alarm snaps into comedy when Daon grabs her phone and protests that the screen will melt and she is still paying it off. After that, the scene slows into ceremony at a much smaller scale. Vesper treats a single touchscreen checkmark as a family crest and asks whether stroking twice would double the vow. He draws one checkmark with calligraphic care. Daon's muttered joke lands, and his composed answer reveals that this is the first pledge he has ever made to a human. The scene ends on an emotional leak he cannot hide: his flame blinks pink twice. There is embarrassment at leaning on a human, and beneath it something larger that he leaves unnamed. The humor comes from the mismatch between a wax seal and a monthly installment plan. The warmth comes from how seriously he fills an empty box.
plan.staging:
Continuous with the previous scene. The setting is the quiet morning maintenance area among covered parade floats, before the park lights come on. Only Vesper (c1) and Daon (c3) are present. Kandra (c2) is referenced only through the wax and must not appear.

Height and reach: Vesper is about two meters tall and Daon is in the low 160s cm. The phone must still be within reach of Vesper's hand and in his view when he checks the box. Who adjusts height is left to the artist.

Extinguisher: Vesper sets it down at the start. After that, both of his hands are free of it.

Wax and gloves: The wax bead is on his bare left index fingertip and is brought near the flame inside his glass lamp head. Later, he puts his glove back on. The checkmark is made with his right index finger, which is gloved.

Daon's phone: Daon holds it throughout. She hugs it to her chest and retreats two steps. She then brings it back out for the checkmark, so the distance between them closes again at some point.

Flame colors: Two flame-color changes are given by the source and should read clearly. The first is a trembling cool blue when he freezes. The second is two pink blinks at the end, while his posture and words stay composed.

The screen: When shown, it displays one small square box that ends up containing a single straight checkmark. The previous scene's condition line is not quoted in this excerpt. Do not letter any screen text. Leave the line as unlettered shape, or keep it out of legible view.

Lettering: Vesper has no mouth, so his balloons point to his glass lamp head. No earpiece or staff-radio transmission occurs in this excerpt, so no radio transmission bands are used.
uncertainties: The speaker of ch-3-p-13 is not named in the source. Attribution to Daon (c3) is inferred, because she is the only other person present and the owner of the phone.

What happens to the wax bead after Vesper freezes is not stated. It is unclear whether it melted, was discarded or was put away. He puts his glove back on, but whether the wax is still on that finger is unspecified.
How much the wax actually melted before Daon stopped him is not stated. Do not show wax dripping onto the phone.
Whether Daon still holds the convenience-store coffee from the previous scene is not stated.
The source does not explain how or whether a gloved finger registers on the touchscreen. It only states that the fingertip touched the screen and a checkmark was drawn. Do not add mechanics.
The exact moment Daon brings the phone back toward Vesper after retreating is not specified.
The unnamed feeling in ch-3-p-25 must stay unnamed. Do not label or visually symbolize it beyond the source-given pink blinks.
Pink is not part of Vesper's established flame color code. It is given only by this source unit and should not be reinterpreted as a specific coded emotion.
Vesper's flame color at the start of the scene, before the blue cooling, is not stated.

beats.action: Vesper sets down the extinguisher, bares his left hand, and brings the bead of the Lady's wax on his fingertip toward his own head flame in earnest.
Daon asks what he is doing. Vesper calmly explains the melting ritual and his plan to press the wax onto the black plate. The threat to the phone becomes clear.
Daon panics, hugs the phone to her chest and retreats two steps. Vesper freezes with the wax raised, and his flame trembles and cools to blue.
Vesper hesitantly asks whether he was rude. Daon reframes the problem as repair costs and redirects him to the empty square box, miming a simple swipe.
Vesper regards the small empty box as if it were a crest waiting to be engraved. He regloves, steadies himself, and hovers his right index finger over the screen.
Before touching the screen, Vesper asks about the protocol: one stroke or two, and whether two would double the vow. Daon flatly answers once.
Vesper's fingertip makes contact and travels very slowly from corner to corner, leaving one straight checkmark. Daon leans in and mutters about brush calligraphy.
Vesper answers composedly that this is his first pledge to a human and cannot be crooked, but his flame betrays him by blinking pink twice. A quiet unnamed feeling closes the scene.

facts.statement: Vesper carefully sets down the fire extinguisher and removes his left glove.
A single bead of hardened candle wax sits on the tip of his left index finger. It dripped from the Lady's flame the previous night. The Lady is Kandra (c2), who is not present in this scene.

Vesper brings the wax close to the flame inside his lamp head to half-melt it. He explains that a contract is only made by melting something, and that he intends to press the wax onto the black plate. The black plate is Daon's phone.
Daon stops him and protests that the screen will melt and that she has not finished paying the installments on the phone.
Daon clutches the phone to her chest and steps back two paces. Vesper freezes while still holding the wax. His flame trembles and cools to blue.
Vesper asks whether he was rude. Daon replies that it is not rudeness but repair costs. She says no seal is needed; he only has to check the small square box on the screen with a swipe of his finger.
To Vesper, the empty square feels like a place to engrave a family crest. He puts his glove back on, steadies his breath, and hovers his right index finger above the screen.
Vesper asks whether the stroke must be made in one go and whether two strokes would double the vow. Daon answers that it is once, just once.
His fingertip touches the screen and moves very slowly from corner to corner, drawing one straight, tidy checkmark. Daon leans in to look and mutters.
Daon remarks that he writes a checkmark like brush calligraphy. Vesper replies that this is the first pledge he has ever made to a human, so it cannot be crooked.

Vesper speaks calmly, but his flame blinks pink twice. He feels somewhat ashamed at having come to rely on a human. Something slightly larger than that shame is also present, and he does not give it a name.

moments.action: Vesper, extinguisher resting at his feet, holds his bare left fingertip with a hardened wax bead close to his glass lamp flame; Daon, phone in hand, stares up startled.
Daon, two steps back, hugs her phone to her chest, shouting in panic; Vesper stands frozen with wax fingertip raised, his lamp flame trembling cool blue.
Vesper tilts his lamp head hesitantly; Daon holds her phone out toward him, fingertip pointing at one small empty square box on the plain screen.
Vesper, both hands gloved, holds his right index finger hovering just above the empty square on Daon's phone, solemn and poised; Daon answers flatly.
Vesper's gloved right fingertip rests on the screen beside one straight, tidy checkmark inside the square; Daon peers in closely, deadpan, muttering.
Vesper stands upright and composed, answering Daon calmly, while his lamp flame flashes bright pink.
Quiet closing beat: Vesper stands still and silent beside Daon, his lamp flame glowing softly, her phone showing the checked square.

units.text: 다온이 메모장 맨 위에 한 줄을 더 적었다.
"계약서엔 이름 있어야죠. 성함이요. 가로등 신사 말고."
"베스퍼요."
"베스퍼 씨."
그녀가 한 글자씩 쳤다. 커피를 한 모금 마시고는 목소리를 낮췄다.
"그럼 이제 말해 줘요. 왜 여기 있어요? 어제 그거, 멀어지면 꺼지는 거. 그거 뭐예요?"
베스퍼는 등 뒤를 의식했다. 보이지 않는 실이 여전히 한쪽으로 팽팽하게 당겨져 있었다. 퍼레이드 동선 위의 그 자리 쪽이었다.
"가을 축제가 끝나는 날까지, 나는 이 자리를 떠날 수 없소."
"……그게 다예요?"
"지금 드릴 수 있는 것은 그것이 다요."
다온은 입을 열었다가 닫았다. 무전기 안테나를 엄지로 두 번 튕기더니 한숨처럼 웃었다.
"도와 달라는 말은 안 하시네요."
도와 달라. 인간의 말로는 그렇게 짧은 것이었다. 베스퍼는 그 말을 목 아래 빈 어딘가에서 굴려 보다가 삼켰다. 문지기는 문 앞에 서는 자였다. 누군가에게 곁에 서 달라고 청하는 자가 아니었다.
"분부를 받들겠소."
"……네, 뭐. 그것도 대답이긴 하죠."

plan.intent: A quiet exchange in which a contract gains a name but loses an answer. The scene opens in the brisk register of paperwork: Daon, still thinking in forms, needs a real name for the contract rather than a stage role, and Vesper gives it plainly. Once the name is typed, she lowers her voice and asks what she actually wants to know, including the fading she witnessed yesterday. The reader should feel the tug Vesper feels, an invisible pull toward the spot on the parade route that nobody else can sense. His answer is honest but closed: he cannot leave until the autumn festival ends, and that is all he can give for now. Daon's reaction carries the emotional turn. She starts to push, stops, flicks her radio antenna twice and laughs like a sigh. Then she names what is missing: he never asks for help. Vesper privately turns those two short human words over and swallows them, because a gatekeeper stands at the gate and does not ask anyone to stand beside him. What comes out instead is formal obedience that calls her instructions a command. Daon accepts it with dry resignation. It is an answer, but not the one she opened the door for. The warmth is small and costly. She stays on his side without being let in, and he leans on her without saying so. There is also an unspoken irony for later: asking for help is something neither of them can do first.
plan.staging:
Continuous with the previous scene. The setting is the quiet morning maintenance area among tarp-covered parade floats, in morning light. Do not use a dusk sky; the previous review flagged a dusk-orange sky as an error. Only Vesper (c1) and Daon (c3) are present. Kandra (c2) does not appear.

Daon's props: she has her phone, used as the memo and typed on character by character; a coffee, which she sips once before lowering her voice; and a staff radio with an antenna, which she flicks twice with her thumb. She wears the navy staff jacket. The memo screen text is not quoted in the source. Do not letter anything on the phone screen. Keep the screen as unlettered shapes or out of legible view.

The pull behind Vesper: the source calls it invisible. It is a sensation, not a visible object. Show only that Vesper is aware of something behind him, oriented toward one direction: the spot on the parade route. Do not draw a literal thread, rope or glowing line. Do not depict the gate or its appearance, since the source gives none here.

Swallowing the words: the source places the unspoken phrase in the empty space below his neck. The established design has empty darkness below his collar. Any showing of that moment must stay wordless and must not invent a visible mechanism.

plan.intent: A small workplace comedy about fitting a human tool to a body that was never built for it. Daon arrives in her brisk manager mode, holding out a tiny earpiece that will let her send him cues during the parade. Her confidence runs straight into a design problem: where a human would have an ear, beside Vesper's glass shade, there is nothing at all. Her pitch stalls in mid-sentence, and the reader should feel that small stop with her. Her deadpan question gets an earnestly puzzled counter-question from Vesper, who honestly does not see why an ear should be required. The fix is improvised and slightly absurd. The earpiece ends up cable-tied to the brass ring on the rim of his shade. Daon presses her forehead at the sight. Vesper, entirely sincere, receives it as the bestowal of an ornament. The comedy runs on two readings of one object. For her it is a patched-together work tool. For him it is a gift of honor. This is the first piece of her equipment he wears, and it is the channel through which her cues, and her worry, will reach him from now on.

plan.intent: The night parade explodes into music and light, and inside that noise the scene closes down to a private, whispered exchange between the two lamp-headed performers walking side by side. Vesper has deliberately kept his flame low because of a promise made that morning. He is relieved to see Kandra's flame standing upright tonight. Kandra, playful and more perceptive than he expects, notices the dimness at once. She teases him in a mock version of his own archaic register, asking whether he ate something bad or promised someone something. His guarded counter-question shows she hit the mark. Her answer lands the joke: his light keeps paying attention to his right ear, and he does not even have an ear. The punchline is immediately confirmed from outside, because the earpiece crackles and Daon's clipped, urgent voice warns that the selfie zone is three minutes away. The reader should feel three pressures at once. There is the public spectacle, the private tenderness of two beings reading each other's light, and the human workplace clock tightening around them. Daon's warning arrives through the signature radio band, as the first live use of the tool fitted in the previous scene.

beats.action: The parade starts at 8:20 PM. Music and light flood the route, and the spectacle is at full volume.

Within the spectacle, Vesper walks the route with his flame deliberately held low because of the morning promise. Beside him Kandra walks, waving a candle, her flame standing straight. He takes quiet relief from seeing her steady.

Without breaking her performance, Kandra slips him a whispered tease: he is dark tonight. Then she prods, mimicking his old-fashioned speech, at the two likely causes, something he ate or something he promised.
Vesper's hesitant, formal counter-question gives him away. Kandra points out the tell: his light keeps attending to his right ear, an ear he does not have.
As if on cue, the earpiece crackles. Daon's rapid, clipped transmission breaks into the private moment: the selfie zone is three minutes away. The workplace clock now presses on both performers.

facts.statement: At 8:20 PM the parade begins: music bursts out and lights pour down.
Vesper walks along the parade route. He has kept his light lowered, mindful of the promise made that morning.
Kandra walks beside him, waving a candle. Tonight her flame stands straight. Seeing that, Vesper is a little relieved.
Kandra whispers to Vesper, addressing him as gentleman, that he is rather dark tonight. The narration says she whispered while moving only the corners of her mouth.
Kandra asks, in an archaic register echoing his own speech, whether he ate something wrong in the morning, or promised someone something.
Vesper, after a pause, asks how the lady knows.
Kandra answers that his light has kept paying attention to his right ear for a while now, even though he has no ear.
The in-ear earpiece crackles. Daon's voice, fast and short, tells Vesper that the selfie zone is coming up in three minutes, repeating the three minutes.

units.text: 셀카존 난간 앞에서 관객들이 휴대폰을 들어 올렸다. 베스퍼는 불빛을 한 톤 더 가라앉혔다. 렌즈마다 흐릿한 주황 번짐이 번졌다. 그때였다.
맨 앞줄의 젊은 여자가 난간 위로 몸을 기울였다. 한 손에는 휴대폰을 들고, 다른 손을 곧장 뻗어 올렸다. 손끝이 향하는 곳은 등갓이었다. 유리와 불꽃, 그리고 그 아래 아무것도 없는 자리.
"가등 선생님, 머리 한 번만요! 진짜 뜨거운지만!"
한 박자. 손이 난간을 넘었다.
베스퍼의 몸은 이미 반쯤 물러날 준비를 하고 있었다. 물러나면 안무가 깨지고, 깨진 안무는 저 수십 개의 검은 판에 담긴다. 물러나지 않으면 손이 유리에 닿는다. 진짜로 뜨겁다는 것이, 진짜로 비어 있다는 것이 들킨다.
두 박자. 인이어가 한 번 치직 하고 끊겼다. 다온은 말이 없었다. 안전요원을 부르는 무전이 들려야 할 자리가 비어 있었다.
세 박자.
'베스퍼 씨, 손! 손, 손등 인사요! 지금, 지금요!'
그 목소리를 듣자마자 베스퍼는 더 생각하지 않았다. 분부였다.
그는 뻗어 오는 손을 향해 오른손을 내밀었다. 느리고 정확하게. 장갑 낀 손바닥이 여자의 손끝을 아래에서 받쳤다. 등갓까지 한 뼘 남은 자리에서 손은 방향을 잃고 장갑 위에 얹혔다. 베스퍼는 허리를 굽혔다. 무도회에서 수백 번 해 온 각도였다. 등갓이 그 손등 위로 기울었고, 입맞춤 대신 따뜻한 불빛이 손등을 스쳤다.
여자의 입이 벌어졌다. 비명이 터졌다. 좋은 쪽으로.
"미쳤다, 손등 인사 해 줬어!"
"저 탈 안에 무용 전공자 있다니까!"
셀카존이 환호로 들썩였다. 불빛이 두 단계쯤 치솟으려 했다. 베스퍼는 그것을 억지로 눌렀다. 옆에서 칸드라가 작게 손뼉을 쳤다. 약속에 없는 박수였다. 촛불이 그를 향해 살짝 기울었다가 곧 제자리로 섰다.
인이어에서 다온이 숨을 몰아쉬는 소리가 났다. 그 위로 다른 목소리가 겹쳤다.
'한다온 씨. 방금 접촉 건, 호출 왜 안 했어요?'

plan.intent: A three-count crisis at the selfie-zone railing, resolved by one courtly gesture. The reader should feel the trap tighten beat by beat. A fan's bare hand is heading for Vesper's hot, hollow glass shade while dozens of phone lenses watch. If he retreats, the choreography breaks on camera. If he stays, the hand touches the truth. Then the one lifeline, the earpiece, crackles and goes dead. The silence is the scariest moment. Daon's frantic order breaks it, and Vesper obeys without thinking because he treats her words as a command. He turns a near-exposure into a ballroom hand-greeting that the crowd adores. The relief is real but costs something. Vesper has to force down his rising light, Kandra gives applause that was never rehearsed, and the page ends with an unseen second voice on the channel asking Daon why she never called safety. The rescue has just become a mark on Daon's record. The signature radio bands must make the channel's rhythm unmistakable. It goes silent, then speaks Daon's order, then brings in the stranger's question.
plan.staging:
Setting: the selfie-zone railing on the night parade route, during the 8:20 PM parade. This continues directly from the previous scene's three-minute warning. A railing separates a crowd of ordinary human fans, all holding up phones, from the performers' side. No signage, logos or festival titles appear.

Present: Vesper (c1) stands on the performer side, close enough to the railing that a leaning fan's hand can reach his shade. Kandra (c2) is beside him on the same side; which side is not stated. The young woman is in the front row with a phone in one hand. Daon (c3) is NOT drawn anywhere in this scene. She is present only as sound through the earpiece. Do not place her near the performers or beside any balloon. Uwoo Taerim (c4) does not appear.

Continuity: the small black earpiece is fastened with a plain, unlettered cable tie to the brass ring beside the glass shade. The crack stays on the upper left of the glass. There is no ear or face on either lamp. Vesper's balloons are not needed in this scene, because he speaks no lines.

Light states that are stated: at the opening, Vesper's flame is lowered one more tone, and the raised phone screens show only a blurry orange smear where he is. During the cheering, his light tries to jump brighter and he holds it down, so show strain rather than a bright flare. No emotion color is assigned anywhere. Kandra's flame leans slightly toward Vesper after her clap, then returns upright.

The near-contact: the fan's reaching fingertips must never touch the glass. Vesper's white-gloved right hand supports her fingertips from below, about a hand-span short of the shade, and her hand comes to rest on his glove. He bows in a formal ballroom hand-kiss posture, the shade tilting over the back of her hand. Only warm light washes across her hand; the glass itself does not contact her. Her phone stays in her other hand.

Speakers for unnamed people: text-3 and text-16 belong to the young woman in the front row. text-17 belongs to another fan in the crowd, not the woman and not Kandra. All three use ordinary white balloons with tails to those human extras.

RADIO BANDS: every earpiece or radio transmission uses the episode's signature full-width horizontal transmission band, never a balloon. The band is a near-black strip running edge to edge through the gutter between panels, with a small radio-wave icon at its left end, bold crisp mint-green lettering, a thin glowing mint outline and static noise along its edges. It has no tail. There are three bands, in this order:
(1) An EMPTY band, containing only static and no lettering, placed right after the panel where the earpiece crackles and cuts out. The crackle SFX text-9 sits inside that panel at the earpiece.
(2) text-12, Daon's order, placed right after the panel carrying the third-beat caption.
(3) text-21, the second unfamiliar voice, as the final band under the last panel. It must NOT be a white balloon, and it must NOT be placed beside any drawn character. It is a voice on the channel addressing Daon, not Daon speaking.
Captions text-10, text-19 and text-20 are ordinary caption boxes, not bands.

Lettering precision: copy every text exactly with no added quotation marks. text-7 contains the word meaning 'truly' TWICE, and both occurrences must use the identical first syllable jin. Double-check the second occurrence, before the phrase about being empty; a previous render wrongly changed its first syllable. text-12 keeps all commas and exclamation marks. No speaker names or labels appear in any balloon, caption or band. No other text appears anywhere.

Panel count, sizes and camera choices are the artist's. Height relation: Vesper is about 2 m, Kandra about 175 cm, and the fans are ordinary human height.
uncertainties: Why Daon went silent and why no safety call came (ch-3-p-62) is not stated. Do not depict a cause.

The identity of the second voice in ch-3-p-72 is not stated. It could be a supervisor or another staff member, but that is not given. Do not draw or name this person. Its speaker field is set to narrator only because no character id fits, and it must not be attributed to Daon.

The fans who speak in ch-3-p-59, ch-3-p-68 and ch-3-p-69 are unnamed extras. Their speaker field is narrator for schema reasons only. It is inferred that the woman speaks ch-3-p-68; the speaker of ch-3-p-69 is unspecified.
Which side of the shade holds the earpiece is not stated. The previous scene placed it on Vesper's right as an inference.
Whether Kandra hears the earpiece traffic is not stated.
Kandra's exact position beside Vesper, left or right, is not stated.
Whether any phone captured non-human detail during the greeting is not stated. Show only the orange blur the source describes at the opening, and do not invent a later exposure.
Vesper's inner reaction to the second voice is not stated. Do not assign him a color change, pose or response after the final band.
The source phrase in ch-3-p-67 about the woman's mouth opening applies to the human fan and may be drawn literally. No mouth or face is ever drawn on Vesper or Kandra.

beats.action: The selfie zone is armed with raised phones. Vesper damps his flame one more tone, and the lenses catch only orange blur. Then something happens.
A front-row fan leans over the railing, phone in one hand, the other reaching straight for the glass shade, and calls out her request to touch it.
First beat: the hand crosses the railing. Vesper's body half-prepares to retreat while the double bind closes. A retreat breaks on camera, and staying lets the hand touch hot, empty glass.
Second beat: the earpiece crackles and goes dead. Daon is silent, and no call for safety staff comes. The count reaches three.
Daon's frantic order bursts through the channel. Vesper stops thinking and obeys, because to him it is a command.

Vesper converts the grab into a ballroom greeting. His gloved right palm catches the fingertips from below, a hand-span short of the shade. He bows, and the shade tilts so that warm light, not glass, brushes the back of her hand.
The near-exposure flips into delight. The fan screams happily, and the crowd reads the gesture as a trained dancer inside the costume.
Cheers shake the zone. Vesper forcibly holds his surging light down. Kandra gives a small, unscripted clap, and her flame leans toward him briefly before standing straight again.
Daon's ragged breathing comes over the earpiece, and a second, unfamiliar voice cuts across it, questioning her for not calling in the contact. The cost of the save lands on Daon.

facts.statement: At the selfie-zone railing, spectators raise their phones. Vesper lowers his light one more tone, and a blurry orange smear spreads in every lens.
A young woman in the front row leans over the railing. She holds a phone in one hand and reaches the other hand straight up toward the lamp shade, which is glass and flame with nothing beneath it.
The woman calls him by the fandom nickname and asks to touch his head just once, only to check whether it is really hot.
One beat passes, and her hand crosses over the railing.

Vesper's body is already half ready to pull back. Retreating breaks the choreography, and the break would be recorded on dozens of black screens. Not retreating lets the hand reach the glass and reveals that it is truly hot and truly empty.
Two beats pass. The in-ear earpiece crackles once and cuts out. Daon says nothing. Where a radio call for safety staff should have been heard, there is nothing.
At the third beat, Daon's voice comes through the earpiece urgently, telling Vesper to give a hand-back greeting, now. Hearing it, Vesper stops deliberating, because to him it is a command.

Vesper extends his right hand toward the reaching hand, slowly and precisely. His gloved palm supports the woman's fingertips from below, one hand-span short of the shade. Her hand loses direction and rests on the glove. He bows at an angle he has made hundreds of times at balls. The shade tilts over the back of her hand, and instead of a kiss, warm light brushes across it.
The woman's mouth falls open and she screams in delight. Fans shout that he gave a hand-back greeting, and that there must be a dance major inside that costume.

The selfie zone erupts in cheers. Vesper's light tries to surge about two steps, and he forces it down. Beside him, Kandra claps softly, which was not agreed on. Her candle flame leans slightly toward him, then stands back upright.
In the earpiece, Daon is heard panting. A different voice overlaps on top of it, asking Daon why she did not make a call about the contact just now.

moments.action: At the selfie-zone railing, fans raise phones toward Vesper; his lamp flame burns low, and every phone screen shows a blurry orange smear where he stands.
A young woman in the front row leans over the railing, phone in one hand, her other hand stretched straight up past the railing toward Vesper's glass shade.
Vesper's tall body leans slightly back, half ready to retreat, while her reaching fingers rise toward his shade beneath dozens of raised black phone screens.
Close on Vesper's shade: the small black earpiece, cable-tied to the brass ring, crackles with a spark of static.
Her fingertips hang a hand-span below Vesper's glowing shade; Vesper stands frozen upright, the crowd's phones still raised.

Vesper bows in ballroom hand-kiss posture, white-gloved right palm supporting her fingertips from below, his shade tilted over the back of her hand, warm light washing across it; her phone in her other hand.
The young woman's mouth falls open in a delighted scream, phone clutched in her hand, fans around her cheering with phones held high.
The selfie zone cheers; Vesper's flame strains yet stays dim. Beside him Kandra claps softly, her candle flame leaning slightly toward him.

units.text: 퍼레이드가 끝난 뒤, 정비 구역 천막 뒤였다. 베스퍼는 덮개 사이 그늘에 서서 다온이 선임 앞에서 고개를 숙이는 것을 보았다. 선임은 태블릿을 들고 있었다.
"매뉴얼 알잖아요. 고객이 공연자 접촉 시도하면 즉시 안전요원 호출, 공연자 분리. 근데 무전이 한 번도 안 떴어요. 3, 4초 비었죠?"
"선임님, 죄송합니다. 제가 판단이 늦었어요. 제 실수예요."
"결과는 괜찮았어요. 근데 결과가 괜찮은 거랑 절차는 별개예요. 알죠?"
"네. 알아요. 죄송합니다."
선임이 화면을 몇 번 두드렸다. 베스퍼 쪽에서는 화면이 보이지 않았다. 대신 다온의 입술이 그 글자를 따라 움직이는 것이 보였다. 고객 접촉 대응 지연.
선임이 떠나고 다온이 천막 뒤로 왔다. 손에는 편의점 봉지가 들려 있었다. 그녀는 이온음료 하나를 꺼내 베스퍼에게 내밀다가, 마실 입이 없다는 걸 떠올리고 소화기 옆에 세워 두었다.
"그냥 거기 둬요. 소화기 친구 하라고."
"다온 님. 방금 그것은."
"근무일지요. 한 줄 남았어요. 괜찮아요, 한 줄이에요."
그녀가 자기 몫의 음료 뚜껑을 비틀었다.
"한 줄."
같은 말을 두 번 했다. 베스퍼는 그녀가 같은 말을 두 번 할 때가 어떤 때인지 오늘 아침부터 알아 가는 중이었다.

plan.intent: This is the quiet price of the selfie-zone save. After the parade, Vesper watches from hiding as the rescue he survived becomes Daon's fault. She takes the blame without a word about why she hesitated. The reader should feel the imbalance: an in-person scolding about a procedure, a record written on a screen Vesper cannot see, and the words readable only on Daon's lips. Then Daon deflects with small kindness and a joke. She brings a drink for someone with no mouth and makes light of it. Vesper tries to ask, formally and haltingly. Daon shrinks the cost to 'one line.' She says it twice, and the scene ends on Vesper's dawning understanding that repetition is her tell. The warmth rests visibly on what Daon quietly absorbed. The tone is subdued after the parade glow: a tent's shadow, a fire extinguisher, a plastic convenience-store bag, and no radio traffic.
plan.staging:
Setting: behind a tent in the maintenance area, after the night parade has ended. The parade glow is gone. Tarp covers hang around the spot, and there is a pocket of shade between them. A fire extinguisher stands nearby. No signage, logos, labels or festival titles appear anywhere.

Present in the first half: Vesper (c1) stands hidden in the shade between the tarps, watching. Daon (c3) stands facing her senior with her head bowed. The senior is an unnamed ordinary human staff member holding a tablet. It is not stated whether the senior or Daon notices Vesper during the scolding, so do not show either looking at him. Kandra (c2) and Uwoo Taerim (c4) do not appear.

Tablet: the screen faces away from Vesper's side and stays unreadable and unlettered. Caption text-9 is the words Vesper reads off Daon's moving lips. It is an ordinary caption box, not screen text and not a balloon. Do not render these words on the tablet.

Speakers: text-2 and text-4 belong to the senior, in ordinary white balloons with tails to the senior. Their speaker field is narrator only for schema reasons. text-3 and text-5 belong to Daon. After the senior has left, Daon comes to Vesper behind the tent. text-10, text-12 and text-13 are Daon's balloons. text-11 is Vesper's balloon, with its tail pointing to his glass lamp head, because he has no mouth.

Drink handling, in stated order: Daon carries a plain, unlettered convenience-store plastic bag. She takes out one ion-drink bottle and begins to hold it out toward Vesper. She stops, remembering that he has no mouth, and stands the bottle upright beside the fire extinguisher instead. text-10 follows this action. Later she twists open the cap of her own drink, a second bottle from the bag, and text-13 follows. Both bottles and the extinguisher carry no lettering.

Continuity: Vesper wears the same tailcoat and white gloves as before. The crack stays on the upper left of the glass shade. The earpiece remains fastened by a plain cable tie to the brass ring beside the shade. Daon wears the navy staff jacket and radio, with her hair tied half-up and the mole at the end of her right eyebrow. No light color or brightness change for Vesper is stated in this scene, so do not assign one.

RADIO BANDS: no earpiece or radio transmission occurs in this scene. Every line is spoken in person, so no transmission bands are drawn. All speech uses ordinary white balloons, and all captions use ordinary caption boxes.

Lettering: copy every text exactly, with no added quotation marks. No speaker names or labels appear anywhere. No other text appears. Panel count, sizes and cameras are the artist's choice.
uncertainties: The senior is unnamed and their rank is not given beyond 'senior.' Whether this is the same second voice heard on the channel at the end of the previous scene is not stated, so do not signal a link.
Whether the senior or Daon notices Vesper watching from the shade during the scolding is not stated.
The source does not state Vesper's emotional reaction or any flame color or brightness change during this scene. Leave his light at a neutral, unremarked state and do not invent one.
ch-3-p-78 says Daon's lips followed the words. It is not stated whether she voiced them aloud. Treat the mouthing as silent, which is the reading implied by Vesper seeing rather than hearing it.
Where Daon went between the senior's departure and her arrival, and where she bought the drinks, is not stated. Show only that she arrives carrying the bag.
Whether Vesper was about to accept the drink with his hand is not stated. Only Daon's offer and her self-correction are given.
What 'the same words twice' has meant earlier today (ch-3-p-85) is not specified in this excerpt. Do not depict a flashback or explain its meaning.

beats.action: Setting shift from parade glare to post-parade shadow. From the gap between tarps, Vesper watches Daon, head bowed, facing a senior who holds a tablet.
The senior lays out the manual rule and the missing radio call. Daon immediately takes the blame as her own mistake.
The senior separates the good result from the broken procedure. Daon agrees and apologizes again.
The senior taps the tablet. The screen is turned away from Vesper, and the entry can be read only on Daon's silently moving lips. The mistake becomes a record.

The senior is gone. Daon arrives with a convenience-store bag and starts to offer Vesper a drink, then catches herself because he has no mouth. She parks the drink beside the fire extinguisher and covers the moment with a joke.
Vesper tries to ask about what he witnessed. Daon names it plainly as the work log and minimizes it: one line, it's fine.
Daon twists open her own drink and says 'one line' again. The repetition registers with Vesper as a tell he has been learning to read since this morning.

facts.statement: After the parade, behind a tent in the maintenance area, Vesper stands in the shade between tarps and watches Daon bow her head before her senior. The senior holds a tablet.

The senior cites the manual. When a guest attempts contact with a performer, staff must immediately call safety staff and separate the performer. The senior points out that no radio call came and that three to four seconds went empty.
Daon apologizes, calls it her own late judgment and her own mistake, and agrees that she knows the rule.
The senior says the outcome was fine, but a good outcome is separate from procedure.
The senior taps the screen several times. Vesper cannot see the screen from where he stands. Instead he sees Daon's lips silently follow the words being entered, which are given in text-9.

After the senior leaves, Daon comes behind the tent carrying a convenience-store bag. She takes out an ion drink and starts to hold it out to Vesper, then remembers he has no mouth to drink with. She stands it beside the fire extinguisher instead.
Daon jokes that the drink can stay there and keep the fire extinguisher company.
Vesper begins to ask about what just happened. Daon answers that it was the work log, that one line was left in it, and that it is fine because it is only one line.
Daon twists open the cap of her own drink and repeats the words meaning 'one line.'
She has said the same thing twice. Since this morning, Vesper has been learning what kind of moment it is when she repeats herself.

brief.style: Full-color Korean romance-fantasy webtoon, clean expressive linework, soft cel shading, subdued post-parade night palette in tent shade, ordinary white balloons and plain caption boxes.

moments.action: Behind a maintenance tent after the parade, Vesper stands half-hidden in shade between hanging tarps, watching Daon bow her head before an ordinary human senior staffer holding a tablet.
The senior, tablet in hand, lays out the rule; Daon bows lower, owning the mistake. Balloon text-2 tails to the senior, text-3 to Daon.
The senior speaks evenly; Daon, head still lowered, answers quietly. Balloon text-4 tails to the senior, text-5 to Daon.
The senior taps the tablet, its blank back turned toward Vesper's side; Daon's lips move silently. Captions read in order text-7, text-6, text-8, text-9.
Daon, now alone with Vesper and holding a plain plastic bag, sets an unlabeled ion-drink bottle upright beside the fire extinguisher, smiling lightly as she jokes.
Vesper turns his glass lamp head toward Daon; she answers him plainly, bag in hand. Balloon text-11 tails to his lamp head, text-12 to Daon.
Daon twists the cap off her own unlabeled bottle, saying text-13 softly; Vesper watches her, the parked bottle standing beside the extinguisher.

units.text: "그 세 박자 동안 다온 님이 호출을 하셨다면."
"안전요원이 왔겠죠. 베스퍼 씨를 뒤로 빼고, 관객이랑 떼어 놓고. 근데 그 사이에 그분 손이 멈췄을 수도 있고, 등갓을 쳤을 수도 있고요."
다온이 어깨를 으쓱했다.
"3초 동안 그 계산 하느라 늦은 거예요. 제가."
베스퍼는 그제야 알았다. 아침에 그은 체크 하나가 무엇을 걸었는지. 그가 불빛을 한 번 잘못 튀기면, 동선을 한 번 벗어나면, 그 대가는 그의 불꽃이 아니라 저 태블릿 속 한 줄로 쌓인다. 다온의 이름 아래에.
불빛이 푸르게 식었다가 한참 뒤에야 주황으로 돌아왔다. 베스퍼는 정식으로 허리를 숙였다.
"사죄하오. 그리고 제안이 있소."
"사람들이 이 몸에게 다가오는 까닭은 이 몸이 너무 반갑게 구는 탓이오. 그러니 덜 반가운 것이 되겠소. 셀카에 응하지 않고, 손을 흔들지 않고, 예를 표하지 않는 것. 재미없는 인형탈."
다온이 그를 한참 올려다보았다. 무전기를 만지작거리던 손이 멈췄다.
"베스퍼 씨가요? 인사를 안 한다고요? 셀카를 거절한다고요?"
"……노력하겠소."
"와, 벌써 불안해."
그러면서도 그녀는 휴대폰을 꺼냈다. 아침의 그 메모장이었다. 체크 하나 아래에 새 줄이 생겼다.

plan.intent: The scene turns the one-line cost into a pact. Vesper asks what would have happened had Daon called for help, and her answer shows him the hidden price of the three seconds she spent calculating. It was a trade between his exposure and her record. The reader should feel the moment his light gives him away, cooling and then slowly recovering, as he understands that his mistakes are stored under her name, not his. His repair is a formal bow and a plan built on his own false belief: become boring, and the cameras will leave. Daon's disbelief is played for comedy, because a gentleman who cannot refuse a selfie is promising to refuse selfies. Still, she writes the plan into the same morning memo and claims it as her own operation for her evaluation score. The scene ends on a partnership that is warm but lopsided. It is funny on the surface, and underneath it rests on what Daon has already absorbed.
